```typescript
/**
 * Co-ownership: editing someone else's element makes you a co-owner, and the
 * element follows its least restricted owner's visibility / lock setting.
 */
import { arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { newElement, newTextElement } from "../newElement";
import { newElementWith } from "../mutateElement";
import {
  CREATOR_ID_KEY,
  EDITOR_IDS_KEY,
  UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
  getCoOwnedCustomData,
  getElementOwnerIds,
  getElementVisibilityBuckets,
  getElementsToCoOwn,
  isElementByHiddenCreator,
  isElementInteractive,
  isOwnershipEdit,
  reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory,
} from "../ownership";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "../types";

const createRect = (creatorId?: string, editorIds?: unknown) =>
  newElement({
    type: "rectangle",
    x: 0,
    y: 0,
    customData: {
      ...(creatorId === undefined ? {} : { [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId }),
      ...(editorIds === undefined ? {} : { [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: editorIds }),
    },
  });

const state = (hidden: string[] = [], locked: string[] = []) => ({
  hiddenCollaboratorIds: new Set(hidden),
  lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(locked),
  collaborators: new Map([
    ["alice-socket", { id: "alice", isCurrentUser: true }],
  ]),
});

describe("owners and buckets", () => {
  it("lists the creator first, then co-owners, without duplicates", () => {
    const rect = createRect("bob", ["carol", "bob", "carol", 42, ""]);
    expect(getElementOwnerIds(rect, arrayToMap([rect]))).toEqual([
      "bob",
      "carol",
    ]);
  });

  it("an untagged element edited by someone is owned by unknown + them", () => {
    const rect = createRect(undefined, ["carol"]);
    expect(getElementOwnerIds(rect, arrayToMap([rect]))).toEqual([
      UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID,
      "carol",
    ]);
  });

  it("bound text follows its container's owners", () => {
    const container = createRect("bob", ["carol"]);
    const text = newTextElement({
      text: "label",
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      containerId: container.id,
    });
    expect(getElementOwnerIds(text, arrayToMap([container, text]))).toEqual([
      "bob",
      "carol",
    ]);
  });

  it("owners this client never saw share the miscellaneous bucket", () => {
    const rect = createRect("bob", ["dave", "erin"]);
    const directory = new Map([["bob", {}]]);
    expect(
      getElementVisibilityBuckets(rect, arrayToMap([rect]), directory),
    ).toEqual(["bob", UNKNOWN_CREATOR_ID]);
  });
});

describe("least restricted owner rule", () => {
  // the example from the feature request: Alice has Bob locked but not
  // Carol, and Carol edited Bob's element
  const rect = createRect("bob", ["carol"]);
  const map = arrayToMap([rect]);

  it("Bob locked, Carol not → interactive for Alice", () => {
    expect(isElementInteractive(rect, map, state([], ["bob"]))).toBe(true);
  });

  it("Bob and Carol both locked → not interactive", () => {
    expect(isElementInteractive(rect, map, state([], ["bob", "carol"]))).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });

  it("Bob hidden, Carol visible → visible and interactive", () => {
    expect(isElementByHiddenCreator(rect, map, state(["bob"]))).toBe(false);
    expect(isElementInteractive(rect, map, state(["bob"], ["bob"]))).toBe(true);
  });

  it("Bob hidden, Carol locked → visible but not interactive", () => {
    expect(isElementByHiddenCreator(rect, map, state(["bob"]))).toBe(false);
    expect(
      isElementInteractive(rect, map, state(["bob"], ["bob", "carol"])),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it("Bob and Carol both hidden → hidden and not interactive", () => {
    expect(isElementByHiddenCreator(rect, map, state(["bob", "carol"]))).toBe(
      true,
    );
    expect(isElementInteractive(rect, map, state(["bob", "carol"]))).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });

  it("an element I co-own can't be locked for me", () => {
    const mine = createRect("bob", ["alice"]);
    expect(
      isElementInteractive(mine, arrayToMap([mine]), state([], ["bob"])),
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  it("without co-owners the creator alone decides (unchanged behaviour)", () => {
    const bobs = createRect("bob");
    expect(
      isElementInteractive(bobs, arrayToMap([bobs]), state([], ["bob"])),
    ).toBe(false);
    expect(
      isElementByHiddenCreator(bobs, arrayToMap([bobs]), state(["bob"])),
    ).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("isOwnershipEdit", () => {
  const rect = createRect("bob");

  it("moving or restyling is an edit", () => {
    expect(isOwnershipEdit(rect, newElementWith(rect, { x: 5 }))).toBe(true);
    expect(
      isOwnershipEdit(rect, newElementWith(rect, { strokeColor: "#f00" })),
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  it("bookkeeping, z-order and binding references are not", () => {
    expect(
      isOwnershipEdit(
        rect,
        newElementWith(rect, {
          index: "a5" as any,
          boundElements: [{ id: "arrow", type: "arrow" }],
          customData: { foo: 1 },
        }),
      ),
    ).toBe(false);
  });

  it("deep-equal copies (like store snapshots) are not edits", () => {
    const line = newElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0 });
    const copy = { ...line, groupIds: [...line.groupIds] };
    expect(isOwnershipEdit(line, copy as ExcalidrawElement)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("getElementsToCoOwn", () => {
  const appState = (selected: string[]) => ({
    selectedElementIds: Object.fromEntries(selected.map((id) => [id, true])),
    collaborators: new Map([["me-socket", { id: "me", isCurrentUser: true }]]),
  });

  const edit = (element: ExcalidrawElement) =>
    newElementWith(element, { x: element.x + 10 });

  it("a selected, edited element someone else created gets me as co-owner", () => {
    const rect = createRect("bob");
    const result = getElementsToCoOwn(
      arrayToMap([rect]),
      arrayToMap([edit(rect)]),
      appState([rect.id]),
    );
    expect(result.map((el) => el.id)).toEqual([rect.id]);
  });

  it("an element changed as a side effect (not selected) doesn't", () => {
    const rect = createRect("bob");
    expect(
      getElementsToCoOwn(
        arrayToMap([rect]),
        arrayToMap([edit(rect)]),
        appState([]),
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("elements I already own don't", () => {
    const mine = createRect("me");
    const coOwned = createRect("bob", ["me"]);
    expect(
      getElementsToCoOwn(
        arrayToMap([mine, coOwned]),
        arrayToMap([edit(mine), edit(coOwned)]),
        appState([mine.id, coOwned.id]),
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("new, deleted, unstamped or merely re-indexed elements don't", () => {
    const fresh = createRect("bob");
    const deleted = createRect("bob");
    const untagged = createRect();
    const reindexed = createRect("bob");
    expect(
      getElementsToCoOwn(
        arrayToMap([deleted, untagged, reindexed]),
        arrayToMap([
          fresh,
          newElementWith(deleted, { isDeleted: true }),
          edit(untagged),
          newElementWith(reindexed, { index: "a9" as any }),
        ]),
        appState([fresh.id, deleted.id, untagged.id, reindexed.id]),
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("editing a label co-owns its shape", () => {
    const container = createRect("bob");
    const text = newTextElement({
      text: "label",
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      containerId: container.id,
    });
    const result = getElementsToCoOwn(
      arrayToMap([container, text]),
      arrayToMap([container, newElementWith(text, { text: "edited" })]),
      { ...appState([]), editingTextElement: text },
    );
    expect(result.map((el) => el.id)).toEqual([container.id]);
  });

  it("does nothing outside of a room (no self id)", () => {
    const rect = createRect("bob");
    expect(
      getElementsToCoOwn(arrayToMap([rect]), arrayToMap([edit(rect)]), {
        selectedElementIds: { [rect.id]: true },
      }),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("getCoOwnedCustomData appends me and keeps other custom data", () => {
    const rect = newElementWith(createRect("bob", ["carol"]), {
      customData: {
        [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "bob",
        [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: ["carol"],
        x: 1,
      },
    });
    expect(getCoOwnedCustomData(rect, "me")).toEqual({
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "bob",
      [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: ["carol", "me"],
      x: 1,
    });
  });
});

describe("reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory", () => {
  it("undo removes me but keeps co-owners added meanwhile", () => {
    const before = createRect("bob", ["me", "carol"]);
    const applied = createRect("bob");
    expect(reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory(before, applied, "me")).toEqual({
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "bob",
      [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: ["carol"],
    });
  });

  it("redo adds me back and keeps everyone else", () => {
    const before = createRect("bob", ["carol"]);
    const applied = createRect("bob", ["me"]);
    expect(reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory(before, applied, "me")).toEqual({
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "bob",
      [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: ["carol", "me"],
    });
  });

  it("history can't bring back someone else who had been removed", () => {
    const before = createRect("bob");
    const applied = createRect("bob", ["carol"]);
    expect(reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory(before, applied, "me")).toEqual({
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "bob",
    });
  });

  it("returns null when history already got it right", () => {
    const before = createRect("bob", ["me"]);
    const applied = createRect("bob");
    expect(reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory(before, applied, "me")).toBeNull();
  });
});
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>

```typescript
/**
 * Co-ownership in the editor: editing a collaborator's element makes you a
 * co-owner, as part of the edit's own undo entry, so undoing every edit you
 * made to it removes you again (and redo puts you back).
 */
import { KEYS } from "@excalidraw/common";
import {
  CREATOR_ID_KEY,
  CaptureUpdateAction,
  EDITOR_IDS_KEY,
  newElementWith,
} from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";
import { getCollaboratorVisibilityRows } from "../scene/visibility";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard } from "./helpers/ui";
import { act, render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

import type { AppState } from "../types";

unmountComponent();

const h = window.h;

const stamp = <T extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  element: T,
  creatorId: string,
  editorIds?: string[],
) =>
  newElementWith(element as ExcalidrawElement, {
    customData: {
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: creatorId,
      ...(editorIds ? { [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: editorIds } : {}),
    },
  }) as T;

const createRect = (id: string, x: number) =>
  API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", id, x, y: 0, width: 10 });

const get = (id: string) => h.elements.find((el) => el.id === id)!;
const editorIdsOf = (id: string) => get(id).customData?.[EDITOR_IDS_KEY];

/** moves the selection right by one step (one undo entry) */
const nudge = () => Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ARROW_RIGHT);

const collaborators = new Map([
  ["my-socket", { id: "me", username: "Me", isCurrentUser: true }],
  ["alice-socket", { id: "alice", username: "Alice" }],
]) as unknown as AppState["collaborators"];

beforeEach(async () => {
  await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  act(() => {
    h.app.updateScene({
      elements: [
        stamp(createRect("alice-rect", 0), "alice"),
        stamp(createRect("me-rect", 40), "me"),
      ],
      collaborators,
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });
    API.setAppState({
      collaboratorDirectory: new Map([
        ["me", { username: "Me", lastSeen: 1 }],
        ["alice", { username: "Alice", lastSeen: 1 }],
        ["carol", { username: "Carol", lastSeen: 1 }],
      ]),
    });
  });
});

describe("becoming a co-owner", () => {
  it("editing a collaborator's element adds me as a co-owner, keeping the creator", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();

    expect(get("alice-rect").x).toBe(1);
    expect(get("alice-rect").customData?.[CREATOR_ID_KEY]).toBe("alice");
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });

  it("selecting without editing doesn't", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("editing my own element doesn't add me as a co-owner", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("me-rect")]);
    nudge();
    expect(editorIdsOf("me-rect")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("editing it again doesn't add me twice", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();
    nudge();
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });

  it("a co-owned element counts for each owner in the menu", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();
    const rows = getCollaboratorVisibilityRows(h.elements, h.state);
    const counts = Object.fromEntries(
      rows.inRoom.map((row) => [row.id, row.drawingsCount]),
    );
    expect(counts).toEqual({ me: 2, alice: 1 });
  });

  it("once I co-own it, locking its creator doesn't lock it for me", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();
    API.setAppState({ lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]) });
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds["alice-rect"]).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("undo / redo", () => {
  it("undoing my only edit removes me as a co-owner, redo adds me back", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(get("alice-rect").x).toBe(0);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toBeUndefined();

    Keyboard.redo();
    expect(get("alice-rect").x).toBe(1);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });

  it("I stay a co-owner until ALL my edits to the element are undone", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();
    nudge();

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(get("alice-rect").x).toBe(1);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(get("alice-rect").x).toBe(0);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("undo keeps co-owners other clients added in the meantime", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();

    // carol edits it too (a remote update, not part of my history)
    act(() => {
      h.app.updateScene({
        elements: h.elements.map((el) =>
          el.id === "alice-rect"
            ? stamp(newElementWith(el, { y: 5 }), "alice", ["me", "carol"])
            : el,
        ),
        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
      });
    });

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(get("alice-rect").x).toBe(0);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["carol"]);

    Keyboard.redo();
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["carol", "me"]);
  });

  it("undoing an unrelated edit doesn't touch my co-ownership", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    nudge();
    API.setSelectedElements([get("me-rect")]);
    nudge();

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(get("me-rect").x).toBe(40);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });
});
```

```bash
describe("becoming a co-owner", () => {
  it("editing a collaborator's element adds me as a co-owner, keeping the creator", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    edit(4);

    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(4);

  });

    API.setSelectedElements([get("me-rect")]);

    edit(4);
    edit(5);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });

  it("a co-owned element counts for each owner in the menu", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    edit(4);
    const rows = getCollaboratorVisibilityRows(h.elements, h.state);

      rows.inRoom.map((row) => [row.id, row.drawingsCount]),
    );
    expect(counts).toEqual({ me: 2, alice: 1 });
  });

  it("once I co-own it, locking its creator doesn't lock it for me", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    edit(4);
    API.setAppState({ lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]) });
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds["alice-rect"]).toBe(true);
  });

  it("without co-owning, locking its creator deselects it (unchanged)", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    API.setAppState({ lockedCollaboratorIds: new Set(["alice"]) });
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds["alice-rect"]).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

describe("undo / redo", () => {
  it("undoing my only edit removes me as a co-owner, redo adds me back", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    const original = widthOf("alice-rect");
    edit(4);

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(original);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toBeUndefined();

    Keyboard.redo();
    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(4);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });

  it("I stay a co-owner until ALL my edits to the element are undone", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    const original = widthOf("alice-rect");
    edit(4);
    edit(5);

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(4);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(original);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it("undo keeps co-owners other clients added in the meantime", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    const original = widthOf("alice-rect");
    edit(4);

    // carol edits it too (a remote update, not part of my history)
    act(() => {
      h.app.updateScene({
        elements: h.elements.map((el) =>
          el.id === "alice-rect"
            ? stamp(newElementWith(el, { y: 5 }), "alice", ["me", "carol"])
            : el,
        ),
        captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
      });
    });

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(original);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["carol"]);

    Keyboard.redo();
    expect(widthOf("alice-rect")).toBe(4);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["carol", "me"]);
  });

  it("undoing an unrelated edit doesn't touch my co-ownership", () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("alice-rect")]);
    edit(4);
    API.setSelectedElements([get("me-rect")]);
    const original = widthOf("me-rect");
    edit(6);

    Keyboard.undo();
    expect(widthOf("me-rect")).toBe(original);
    expect(editorIdsOf("alice-rect")).toEqual(["me"]);
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 01:09:41Z)**_

Co-ownership is in. Editing someone else's element now makes you a co-owner, and the element follows the least restricted of its owners. Undoing every edit you made to an element removes you as a co-owner again, and redo restores you.

**Test status:** the typecheck and lint are clean. The 36 new tests pass. The full suite had 2321 passing and 1 failing: `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx`, the untracked file that was already in your working tree. It fails the same way with my changes stashed, so it isn't caused by this work. I haven't committed anything.

## How it behaves

- **Ownership data:** `customData.creatorId` still records the original creator. A new `customData.editorIds` lists the co-owners.
- **Visibility and lock rule** (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`):

  - An element is hidden only if **every** owner is hidden.
  - It is interactive if **any** owner is interactive.

  Your example works: the owners are {Bob, Carol}, Alice has Bob locked but not Carol, so Alice can interact with it. Everything that decides what's drawn or can be touched (rendering, hit testing, selection, eraser, export, search, arrow binding) goes through these two functions, so it all follows the new rule.

- **What counts as an edit:** any real change to an element you had selected, or to a label you were editing. Changes that happen as a side effect don't count:
  - an arrow rerouted because the shape it's attached to moved,
  - shapes inside a frame you dragged,
  - z-order changes and binding updates.

## How undo works

The co-owner stamp is recorded as part of the edit's own undo step, not a separate one. The editor adds it just before saving the edit to history (`store.ts`, `App.tsx`).

- You're only added on your first edit to an element, so that's the step that adds you.
- Undo goes newest-first, so that step is undone last. You stop being a co-owner exactly when all your edits to the element are undone.
- Redo of that step adds you back.

Undo normally restores the whole `customData` object, which would also remove anyone who became a co-owner after your edit. To prevent that, `history.ts` merges the result after every undo or redo: only your own co-ownership changes, and everyone else's stays as it was. A test covers this: Carol co-owns the element after my edit, I undo, and she remains a co-owner.

## The menu

- **Hide all** also hides co-owners, so co-owned elements don't stay showing.
- A co-owned element is counted in each owner's drawing count, so the counts can add up to more than the number of elements.

## Limitations

- **Arrow-key moves:** the editor doesn't save an arrow-key move as its own undo step; it gets folded into whichever step comes next. You only become a co-owner from an arrow-key move if the element is still selected when that next step is saved. This is existing editor behaviour, which I didn't change.
- **Simultaneous edits:** if two people edit the same element at the same moment, the last save wins for the whole element, so one person's co-ownership can be lost along with their edit.

## Files

- **Changed:** `packages/element/src/ownership.ts`, `packages/element/src/store.ts`, `packages/excalidraw/history.ts`, `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`, `packages/excalidraw/scene/visibility.ts`
- **New tests:** `packages/element/src/__tests__/coOwnership.test.ts` (25 tests on the rules) and `packages/excalidraw/tests/coOwnership.test.tsx` (11 in the editor, including multi-step undo and redo)

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 01:28:57Z)**_

No, the element is not always deleted. Often it comes back, for everyone. Deletion gets no special priority when edits are synced. A delete is an ordinary change that sets `isDeleted: true` and bumps the element's version by one, and it's resolved like any other edit. My co-ownership changes don't affect this.

## The rule (`packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`, `shouldDiscardRemoteElement`)

When a client receives a remote copy of an element it already has, it keeps its **local** copy if any of these is true:

1. The local element is currently being text-edited, resized, or created (`editingTextElement`, `resizingElement`, `newElement`).
2. The local version is higher (`local.version > remote.version`).
3. The versions are equal and the local `versionNonce` is lower or the same. This is a deterministic tiebreak.

Otherwise the remote copy, deleted or not, replaces the local one. So whichever copy has the higher version wins, and every mouse move or keystroke bumps the version.

## What happens in practice

Say Bob is editing an element and Alice deletes it.

| What Bob is doing | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Dragging, resizing or rotating** | Each move bumps Bob's version, so it quickly passes Alice's +1 delete. While resizing, Bob's client also ignores incoming copies entirely (rule 1). Bob keeps broadcasting, and his higher version overwrites the deletion on Alice's screen. **The element reappears for everyone.** |
| **Editing text** | Bob's client ignores Alice's delete while he types (rule 1). When he finishes, his text update usually has the higher version and gets broadcast, so **it comes back**. If he made no change, his version can stay lower. Then the deletion wins once Alice's client sends the full scene again (every ~20s via `queueBroadcastAllElements`) or makes another change. |
| **Just has it selected, not changing anything** | Bob's version doesn't move, so **the deletion wins** and the element disappears for him too. |
| **Edits at almost the same moment, with equal versions** | Decided by the `versionNonce` tiebreak, which is effectively random. **Either outcome is possible.** |

The outcome also depends on timing. If Alice's delete arrives _between_ Bob's edits, Bob's client accepts it, the element disappears under his cursor, and his edit stops. If it arrives while Bob is mid-gesture with a higher version, his edit wins.

One more catch: whoever "loses" can still reverse the result with undo. Undo restores the element with a fresh, higher version. For example, Alice can undo her delete after Bob's edit wins, or Bob can undo after the deletion wins.

## Could deletion be made to always win?

It could, but not by simply always preferring the deleted copy, because undo depends on bringing deleted elements back. Undoing a delete just sets `isDeleted: false` with a higher version. A rule that deletion always wins would make deletes impossible to undo once they had synced.

Two workable options:

- **Deletion wins only while the deleted copy is recent.** Treat a remote delete as winning over local edits made within a short window, and still allow undo to restore the element later.
- **Show a conflict to the editor instead of resolving it silently.** For example, tell Bob "Alice deleted this element" and let him choose whether to restore it.

Both change how editing feels for everyone in the room, so it's a product decision before it's a code one. I can prototype either if you want.

_**User (2026-11-13 01:33:22Z)**_

What are some possible options for changing the current 'last save wins' system, and the pros and cons of each option?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 01:34:04Z)**_

There are three broad approaches: prevent conflicts, resolve them more precisely, or show them to the user. One fact about the current system matters for all of them. `version` is a mutation counter, not a timestamp, so today's rule is really "**the copy changed the most times wins**", not "last save wins". A long drag (hundreds of version bumps) beats a delete (one bump) even if the delete happened later. Some options below fix only that; others go further.

Any replacement must also **converge deterministically**: every client, given the same updates in any order, has to reach the same result. A rule that depends on local state, like the existing "I'm editing it, so ignore remote" rule, is only safe because the local client eventually broadcasts its own copy.

## 1. Time-based ordering (hybrid logical clocks)

Replace the version counter as the tiebreaker with a hybrid logical clock (HLC). This is a timestamp that each client advances past any timestamp it has seen, so it orders events correctly even when device clocks disagree.

- **Pros:** Small change, mostly in `reconcile.ts` plus stamping the clock in `mutateElement`. Fixes "the busiest editor wins": the change made latest in time wins. Delete-during-edit then behaves as people expect.
- **Cons:** It's still whole-element: the losing edit is discarded entirely. Plain wall-clock time would be broken by clock skew, which is why it has to be an HLC. Clients that predate the change don't send the field, so you need a fallback rule.

## 2. Per-property merge

Track a version (or HLC) per property, or per group of properties, instead of per element. Merge property by property.

- **Pros:** Edits to different properties both survive: Carol moves the shape while Dave recolors it. `customData.editorIds` can merge as a set, so simultaneous co-owner stamps stop overwriting each other, which is the limitation I flagged earlier.
- **Cons:** Changes the sync format and the stored scene, with extra metadata on every element. Some properties must stay together (`x`/`y`/`width`/`height`/`points`/`angle`), or a merge can produce shapes nobody drew. Undo then has to restore individual properties, not whole elements. And a plain set union of `editorIds` would undo your rule that undoing all your edits removes you. You'd need an observed-remove set (a set that records removals so a stale copy can't re-add them), not a simple union.

## 3. Soft locks (prevent conflicts instead of resolving them)

When a user starts dragging, resizing or text-editing, broadcast "I'm editing X". Other clients show an indicator and won't let their user edit or delete X until it's released.

- **Pros:** Prevents the conflict instead of picking a loser, which is the best experience for delete-during-edit. Cheap: each collaborator's `selectedElementIds` is already broadcast in the pointer updates, and you already have per-element interactivity checks to hook into (`isElementInteractive`).
- **Cons:** Locks go stale when someone disconnects or leaves something selected, so you need timeouts and release on idle. Two users can grab the same element at the same instant, so you need a tiebreaker. It reduces how freely people can work together. It's also easy to confuse with your existing per-user lock feature, so the naming needs care.

## 4. Targeted rules on top of the current system

Keep whole-element resolution but add specific policies: a deletion wins for N seconds, `customData` is always merged rather than replaced, and so on.

- **Pros:** Small, incremental, testable one rule at a time in `reconcile.ts`.
- **Cons:** Ad hoc: rules interact in non-obvious ways, and each must be checked against undo (restoring a deleted element relies on un-deleting with a higher version) and against deterministic convergence. Rules based on time windows are especially easy to get wrong across clients.

## 5. Conflict detection with a visible prompt

Detect true conflicts (both sides changed the element since a shared earlier version) and tell the user: "Alice deleted this while you were editing it. Restore?"

- **Pros:** Transparent: nothing disappears silently, and the user decides.
- **Cons:** Needs each element's shared earlier version tracked, which the current format doesn't do. Interrupts real-time drawing, and can get noisy in busy rooms. It's a UX layer, not a resolution rule, so it still needs one of the other options underneath.

## 6. Server-assigned ordering

Have the relay server stamp each update with a sequence number, and apply updates in that single global order.

- **Pros:** One unambiguous order, no clock problems, simple rules.
- **Cons:** Requires changing the relay server, and scenes are end-to-end encrypted, so the server can order updates but never read or merge them. Adds latency to every edit. The Firebase saves follow a separate path that would also have to respect the order. Applying updates in a fixed order still doesn't merge them; it only makes the existing rule fairer.

## 7. Replace the sync layer with a CRDT library (Yjs / Automerge)

Model the scene as a CRDT (a data structure that merges concurrent edits automatically): elements as maps, `editorIds` as a set, and so on.

- **Pros:** Proven to converge, merges per property, handles offline edits, and good undo support exists (Yjs `UndoManager`, which undoes only your own changes, matching your co-ownership semantics).
- **Cons:** Effectively rewrites `Collab`, `Portal`, the Firebase storage, `reconcile.ts` and how history ties in. Deleted data and history accumulate and need cleanup. The sizes of the change and its risk are far larger than the rest. Fractional indices for ordering are already partly CRDT-like, and you'd be replacing working code.

## Comparison

| Option | Effort | Fixes delete-during-edit | Keeps both edits | Format change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Time-based ordering (HLC) | Low | Mostly (later action wins) | No | Small (one field) |
| 2. Per-property merge | Medium–High | Partly | Yes (different properties) | Yes |
| 3. Soft locks | Low–Medium | Yes (prevents it) | n/a | No (uses existing presence data) |
| 4. Targeted rules | Low per rule | If you write that rule | Per rule | Usually no |
| 5. Conflict prompt | Medium | Lets the user choose | User's choice | Yes (shared-version tracking) |
| 6. Server ordering | Medium + server work | Only via order, not merge | No | Server protocol |
| 7. CRDT (Yjs/Automerge) | Very high | Yes | Yes | Complete |

## Recommendation

For this codebase I'd combine **3 + 1**, plus a small piece of **2**:

- **Soft locks** prevent the most visible conflicts, like deleting something someone is dragging, cheaply, using presence data you already broadcast. They also fit naturally next to your per-user lock feature.
- **HLC ordering** makes the remaining conflicts resolve by when things happened, not by how much was changed.
- **Merging only `editorIds`**, as a set that records removals, fixes the one known gap in co-ownership without changing how the rest of the element is synced.

A full CRDT migration is only worth it if offline editing or rich merging becomes a core goal.

If this is going to your team, I can turn it into a shareable page.

```text
export const newElementWith = <TElement extends ExcalidrawElement>(
  element: TElement,
  updates: ElementUpdate<TElement>,
  /** pass `true` to always regenerate */
  force = false,
): TElement => {
  let didChange = false;
  for (const key in updates) {
    const value = (updates as any)[key];
    if (typeof value !== "undefined") {
      if (
        (element as any)[key] === value &&
        // if object, always update because its attrs could have changed
        (typeof value !== "object" || value === null)
      ) {
        continue;
      }
      didChange = true;
    }
  }

  if (!didChange && !force) {
    return element;
  }

  return {
    ...element,
    ...updates,
    version: updates.version ?? element.version + 1,
    versionNonce: updates.versionNonce ?? randomInteger(),
    updated: getUpdatedTimestamp(),
  };
};

/**
 * Mutates element, bumping `version`, `versionNonce`, and `updated`.
 *
 * NOTE: does not trigger re-render.
 */
export const bumpVersion = <T extends Mutable<ExcalidrawElement>>(
  element: T,
  version?: ExcalidrawElement["version"],
) => {
  element.version = (version ?? element.version) + 1;
  element.versionNonce = randomInteger();
  element.updated = getUpdatedTimestamp();
  return element;
};
```

```typescript
/**
 * Hybrid logical clock (single-number variant) for element `updated`
 * timestamps, which collaboration uses to decide which concurrent copy of an
 * element wins ("the latest change wins", see `reconcileElements`).
 *
 * - it follows the wall clock (ms since epoch), so timestamps stay meaningful
 *   (e.g. for expiring deleted elements)
 * - it never goes backwards, even if the device clock does
 * - when a remote timestamp is observed, it jumps ahead to it, so a change
 *   made after seeing another client's change is never older than it, even
 *   if this device's clock is behind
 *
 * Instead of a logical counter, equal timestamps are left to the version /
 * versionNonce tie-breaks in `reconcileElements`. Remote timestamps too far
 * ahead of the local wall clock are only adopted up to `maxDriftMs`, so one
 * client with a badly wrong clock can't drag everyone's clock forward.
 */
export class HybridClock {
  private last = 0;

  constructor(
    private readonly now: () => number = Date.now,
    private readonly maxDriftMs = 60 * 1000,
  ) {}

  /** a timestamp for a local change: never lower than any returned/observed */
  tick(): number {
    this.last = Math.max(this.now(), this.last);
    return this.last;
  }

  /** advances the clock to a timestamp seen on a remote element */
  observe(timestamp: unknown) {
    if (typeof timestamp !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(timestamp)) {
      return;
    }
    this.last = Math.max(
      this.last,
      Math.min(timestamp, this.now() + this.maxDriftMs),
    );
  }
}

/** the editor's clock for element `updated` timestamps */
export const elementClock = new HybridClock();
```

```text
export const shouldDiscardRemoteElement = (
  localAppState: AppState,
  local: OrderedExcalidrawElement | undefined,
  remote: RemoteExcalidrawElement,
): boolean => {
  if (
    local &&
    // local element is being edited
    (local.id === localAppState.editingTextElement?.id ||
      local.id === localAppState.resizingElement?.id ||
      local.id === localAppState.newElement?.id ||
      // local element is newer
      local.version > remote.version ||
      // resolve conflicting edits deterministically by taking the one with
      // the lowest versionNonce
      (local.version === remote.version &&
        local.versionNonce <= remote.versionNonce))
  ) {
    return true;
  }
  return false;
};
```

```typescript
/**
 * Collaboration conflict rules:
 * - the latest change wins (hybrid logical clock timestamps in `updated`),
 *   falling back to the version rules for same-ms changes and old data
 * - co-owners (`customData.editorIds`) are merged from both copies
 */
import { HybridClock } from "@excalidraw/common";
import {
  CREATOR_ID_KEY,
  EDITOR_IDS_KEY,
  EDITOR_SEQS_KEY,
  newElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { OrderedExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { reconcileElements } from "../../data/reconcile";

import type { RemoteExcalidrawElement } from "../../data/reconcile";
import type { AppState } from "../../types";

const element = (
  opts: {
    version: number;
    updated?: number;
    versionNonce?: number;
    isDeleted?: boolean;
    editors?: Record<string, { seq: number; present: boolean }>;
  },
  id = "shape",
): OrderedExcalidrawElement => {
  const editors = Object.entries(opts.editors ?? {});
  return {
    ...newElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0 }),
    id,
    index: "a0",
    version: opts.version,
    versionNonce: opts.versionNonce ?? 1,
    updated: opts.updated as number,
    isDeleted: !!opts.isDeleted,
    customData: {
      [CREATOR_ID_KEY]: "bob",
      ...(editors.length
        ? {
            [EDITOR_IDS_KEY]: editors
              .filter(([, e]) => e.present)
              .map(([id]) => id),
            [EDITOR_SEQS_KEY]: Object.fromEntries(
              editors.map(([id, e]) => [id, e.seq]),
            ),
          }
        : {}),
    },
  } as OrderedExcalidrawElement;
};

const noEdit = {} as AppState;

/** reconciles on "my" client and on the other client; both must agree */
const reconcileBothWays = (
  mine: OrderedExcalidrawElement,
  theirs: OrderedExcalidrawElement,
  appState = noEdit,
) => {
  const onMine = reconcileElements(
    [structuredClone(mine)],
    [structuredClone(theirs)] as RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
    appState,
  )[0];
  const onTheirs = reconcileElements(
    [structuredClone(theirs)],
    [structuredClone(mine)] as RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
    noEdit,
  )[0];
  return { onMine, onTheirs };
};

describe("HybridClock", () => {
  it("follows the wall clock", () => {
    let now = 1000;
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => now);
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1000);
    now = 1500;
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1500);
  });

  it("never goes backwards, even if the device clock does", () => {
    let now = 1000;
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => now);
    clock.tick();
    now = 400;
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1000);
  });

  it("jumps ahead to an observed remote timestamp (device clock behind)", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    clock.observe(5000);
    // a change made after seeing the remote one is never older than it
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(5000);
  });

  it("ignores observed timestamps older than its own", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    clock.observe(10);
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1000);
  });

  it("adopts remote timestamps only up to the max drift ahead of the wall clock", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000, 60_000);
    clock.observe(1000 + 3_600_000);
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(61_000);
  });

  it("ignores invalid timestamps", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    clock.observe(undefined);
    clock.observe(NaN);
    clock.observe(Infinity);
    clock.observe("9999");
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1000);
  });
});

describe("reconcileElements — the latest change wins", () => {
  it("a later delete beats an earlier edit with many more versions", () => {
    // Bob dragged the shape (many version bumps) and stopped at t=100;
    // Alice deleted it at t=200 (a single version bump)
    const bobs = element({ version: 50, updated: 100 });
    const alices = element({ version: 6, updated: 200, isDeleted: true });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(bobs, alices);
    expect(onMine.isDeleted).toBe(true);
    expect(onTheirs.isDeleted).toBe(true);
  });

  it("a later edit beats an earlier delete", () => {
    const bobs = element({ version: 7, updated: 300 });
    const alices = element({ version: 6, updated: 200, isDeleted: true });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(bobs, alices);
    expect(onMine.isDeleted).toBe(false);
    expect(onTheirs.isDeleted).toBe(false);
  });

  it("same millisecond: falls back to the higher version", () => {
    const a = element({ version: 9, updated: 200 });
    const b = element({ version: 6, updated: 200, isDeleted: true });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(a, b);
    expect(onMine.version).toBe(9);
    expect(onTheirs.version).toBe(9);
  });

  it("same millisecond and version: the lowest versionNonce wins", () => {
    const a = element({ version: 6, updated: 200, versionNonce: 5 });
    const b = element({
      version: 6,
      updated: 200,
      versionNonce: 2,
      isDeleted: true,
    });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(a, b);
    expect(onMine.versionNonce).toBe(2);
    expect(onTheirs.versionNonce).toBe(2);
  });

  it("old data without timestamps: falls back to the version rules", () => {
    const a = element({ version: 9 });
    const b = element({ version: 6, updated: 500, isDeleted: true });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(a, b);
    expect(onMine.version).toBe(9);
    expect(onTheirs.version).toBe(9);
  });

  it("an element being edited locally still keeps the local copy", () => {
    const mine = element({ version: 7, updated: 100 });
    const theirs = element({ version: 8, updated: 200, isDeleted: true });

    const [result] = reconcileElements(
      [mine],
      [theirs] as RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
      { resizingElement: mine } as unknown as AppState,
    );
    expect(result).toBe(mine);
  });
});

describe("reconcileElements — co-owners are merged", () => {
  const coOwners = (el: OrderedExcalidrawElement) => ({
    ids: el.customData?.[EDITOR_IDS_KEY],
    seqs: el.customData?.[EDITOR_SEQS_KEY],
  });

  it("concurrent co-owner stamps both survive, whichever copy wins", () => {
    const carols = element({
      version: 7,
      updated: 300,
      editors: { carol: { seq: 1, present: true } },
    });
    const daves = element({
      version: 7,
      updated: 200,
      editors: { dave: { seq: 1, present: true } },
    });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(carols, daves);
    const expected = { ids: ["carol", "dave"], seqs: { carol: 1, dave: 1 } };
    expect(coOwners(onMine)).toEqual(expected);
    expect(coOwners(onTheirs)).toEqual(expected);
    // the element's other properties still come from the latest change
    expect(onMine.updated).toBe(300);
    expect(onTheirs.updated).toBe(300);
  });

  it("an undone co-ownership stays removed against a stale copy", () => {
    // my undo removed me (seq 2) but the other copy is a newer edit made
    // before my undo arrived (it still lists me at seq 1)
    const mine = element({
      version: 9,
      updated: 300,
      editors: { me: { seq: 2, present: false } },
    });
    const theirs = element({
      version: 8,
      updated: 400,
      editors: { me: { seq: 1, present: true } },
    });

    const { onMine, onTheirs } = reconcileBothWays(mine, theirs);
    expect(onMine.updated).toBe(400);
    expect(coOwners(onMine)).toEqual({ ids: [], seqs: { me: 2 } });
    expect(coOwners(onTheirs)).toEqual({ ids: [], seqs: { me: 2 } });
  });

  it("merging into the local winner keeps the same element object", () => {
    const mine = element({
      version: 9,
      updated: 300,
      editors: { carol: { seq: 1, present: true } },
    });
    const theirs = element({
      version: 8,
      updated: 200,
      editors: { dave: { seq: 1, present: true } },
    });

    const [result] = reconcileElements(
      [mine],
      [theirs] as RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
      noEdit,
    );
    expect(result).toBe(mine);
    expect(result.version).toBe(9);
    expect(coOwners(result).ids).toEqual(["carol", "dave"]);
  });

  it("doesn't touch elements whose co-owners already match", () => {
    const mine = element({ version: 9, updated: 300 });
    const theirs = element({ version: 10, updated: 400 }, "shape");

    const [result] = reconcileElements(
      [mine],
      [theirs] as RemoteExcalidrawElement[],
      noEdit,
    );
    expect(result).toBe(theirs);
  });
});
```

_**User (2026-11-13 02:10:35Z)**_

With the new changes, If a user is editing an element, and another deletes the element while they are editing, will the element always be deleted?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 02:11:01Z)**_

Still not always. The difference now is that the result depends on **who acted last**, not on who made more changes.

The new rule: whichever copy has the later `updated` timestamp wins. When a client receives _any_ remote change, its clock jumps forward to at least that change's timestamp, even if it ignores the change. So anything the editor does after the delete reaches them gets a later timestamp than the delete. Ties within the same millisecond still fall back to the old version/nonce rule.

Say Bob is editing and Alice deletes.

| What Bob is doing | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Finished editing before Alice deleted** (e.g. dragged, stopped, then she deleted) | Bob usually won, because his drag made far more version bumps | **Deleted.** Her delete is later. This is the main fix. |
| **Just has it selected, no changes** | Deleted | **Deleted** |
| **Still dragging when the delete arrives** | Usually came back | **Comes back** if Bob moves it again after the delete arrives, because his clock is now past the delete. If he holds still, the delete wins and the element disappears from under his cursor. |
| **Resizing, typing in it, or still drawing it** | Came back | **Comes back.** Bob's client still ignores incoming changes to an element he's actively resizing, typing in or drawing. His next change gets a later timestamp, overwrites the delete, and is sent to everyone. If he finishes text editing without changing anything, the delete wins the next time Alice's copy is re-sent (every ~20s). |
| **Edits in the same millisecond** | Version/nonce tie-break | Same tie-break: either outcome is possible |

## Other cases where the result can still surprise you

- **Clock skew before the first exchange.** The clock only orders events correctly once clients have seen each other's changes. If Bob's device clock runs ahead of Alice's and they haven't exchanged any changes yet, an edit he made _before_ her delete can still carry a later timestamp and win. The first exchanged change brings their clocks into line. I cap how far ahead a remote timestamp can drag a clock at 60 seconds, so a clock that is badly wrong can only distort results by up to that much.
- **Undo can bring it back.** Undo and redo create a fresh timestamp, so undoing an edit or a delete counts as a new, latest change.
- **Co-ownership has no effect on deletion.** The `editorIds` merge only combines the list of co-owners. Whether the element is deleted comes from the winning copy like every other property.

## In short

A delete now sticks unless the editor is still actively changing the element after the delete reaches them. That's the "last action wins" behaviour this change was meant to give.

Making a delete stick even against someone who is actively editing would need one of the other options: soft locks (Alice can't delete what Bob is editing), or a prompt telling Bob "this was deleted".

The full test run for this change (typecheck, lint, all tests) is still going in the background. I'll report its result when it finishes.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 02:11:36Z)**_

The two changes are in: concurrent edits are now decided by a clock (the latest change wins), and co-owner lists are merged instead of overwritten. The typecheck and lint are clean. The full suite has 2345 passing tests and 1 failure, in `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx`. That untracked file was already in your working tree and failed the same way before any of my changes. The 16 new reconcile tests pass after I fixed a type cast in that file. I haven't committed anything.

**1. Latest change wins (a timestamp clock, called a hybrid logical clock)**

- **The clock** (`packages/common/src/clock.ts`): it follows the device clock and never goes backwards. When a client sees a change from someone else, its clock jumps forward to at least that change's time, so anything done after seeing it counts as later. It adopts remote times at most 60 seconds ahead of its own device clock.
- **Where the time is stored:** in each element's existing `updated` field (`getUpdatedTimestamp` now reads from this clock). The file format doesn't change, and undo/redo already stamp a fresh time.
- **The rule** (`packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`): the copy with the later `updated` wins. Same millisecond, or old data with no timestamp, falls back to the old rule (higher version, then lowest `versionNonce`). Elements someone is actively resizing, typing in or drawing still keep their local copy.
- **In the existing tests:** `getUpdatedTimestamp` returns `1` in tests, so every timestamp ties and the existing tests still run under the old rule. The new tests set timestamps explicitly.

**2. Co-owner lists are merged** (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`)

- Next to `editorIds`, each element now also stores `customData.editorSeqs`: one counter per client that has ever been a co-owner.
- Each client only ever changes its own counter, so whichever copy has the higher counter for that client is the newer one.
- A removed co-owner keeps their counter as a marker, so an older copy that still lists them can't add them back.
- When copies are reconciled, the co-owner lists are merged, while everything else comes from the winning copy. The merge gives the same result whatever order copies arrive in, and it doesn't bump the element's version, so it doesn't cause extra re-broadcasts.
- Undo/redo give your own entry a new, higher counter, so undoing your last edit removes you, and that removal holds against older copies.

**Things to know**

- **Deploy all clients together.** Clients running the old rule and the new rule could settle on different copies of the same element. Users get the new code by reloading the page, so the risk only lasts as long as someone keeps an old tab open.
- **After an undo, `editorIds` is an empty list, not missing.** The removed co-owner's counter has to stay behind (`editorSeqs: { me: 2 }`), so I updated the earlier tests to expect `[]`.

**New and updated tests**

- **`packages/excalidraw/tests/data/reconcileClock.test.ts` (16, new):** clock behaviour, the latest-change-wins rule, the fallback to the old rule, both clients reaching the same result, and merging co-owner lists.
- **`packages/element/src/__tests__/coOwnership.test.ts` (updated):** now covers the counters, the merge, and undo/redo.
- **`packages/excalidraw/tests/coOwnership.test.tsx` (updated):** now expects the removal marker left after an undo.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 02:27:08Z)**_

Today, three kinds of in-progress edit make a client ignore incoming changes to that element. The check is the first one in `shouldDiscardRemoteElement` (`packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`):

| Local state          | Example                            |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `resizingElement`    | resizing or rotating with a handle |
| `editingTextElement` | typing in a text box or label      |
| `newElement`         | the shape you're still drawing     |

Dragging isn't protected, so incoming changes are already accepted while you drag.

## Why the guard exists

Simply deleting the guard wouldn't make incoming changes stick. Each of these edits keeps its own copy of what it started from:

- **Resizing and rotating** recompute the element on every pointer move from `pointerDownState.originalElements` (`App.tsx:9275`), the copy taken at pointer-down. An accepted change would be overwritten on the next pointer move. You'd see a flicker, and the change would still be lost.
- **Text editing** treats the textarea's contents as the true text. The next keystroke writes the textarea back over any remote text change.
- **Drawing a new shape** rebuilds it from the pointer path on every move.

So "accept incoming changes" means **making the in-progress edit take the incoming change into account**, not just letting it through. One constraint applies to every option: the guard currently produces a consistent result only because the editing client broadcasts its final version when it finishes. Each option below still ends with the editor broadcasting an element that already includes what they accepted, so every client ends up with the same copy.

## Options

### A. Accept only the properties the edit isn't changing

While an edit is in progress, take the remote copy's values for every property that edit doesn't control, and keep the local values for the ones it does:

- **Resizing or rotating** controls `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `angle`, `points` and `scale`.
- **Text editing** controls `text`, `originalText`, and the dimensions that follow from them.
- **Drawing a new shape** controls its geometry.

Apply the result to the local element in place, because the edit holds a reference to it. The co-owner merge already does the same thing.

- **Pros:** Moderate effort, all in `reconcile.ts` plus a table of which properties each edit controls. Handles the common case: someone recolors, restyles, regroups or co-owns the shape while you're resizing it, and both changes survive. Your final broadcast already includes their change, so everyone converges.
- **Cons:** Incoming changes to the properties you're editing are still dropped, including a move while you resize. **Deletion isn't covered**: `isDeleted` needs a decision of its own (option B).

### B. Treat an incoming delete as "cancel my edit"

If a newer remote delete arrives for the element you're editing, accept it, end your edit, and show a notice such as "Alice deleted this shape".

- **Pros:** Deletes always stick, which answers the earlier question directly. The behaviour is easy to explain.
- **Cons:** Each kind of edit needs a cancel path:

  - **Resizing:** clear `resizingElement` and reset `pointerDownState`.
  - **Text editing:** close the text editor without saving.
  - **Drawing:** discard `newElement`.

  The editor also loses whatever they were doing, including typed text. To soften that, keep the lost text (for example, offer it for copying) or let undo restore the element.

### C. Rebase the edit onto the incoming copy

When a remote change to the element you're editing is accepted:

- **Resizing and rotating:** apply the same change to the stored starting copy (`pointerDownState.originalElements`), so later pointer moves start from the new state.
- **Text editing:** merge the remote text into the textarea, either with a three-way text merge or by locking the edited range.
- **Pros:** The richest result: concurrent geometry changes combine, so a move by Alice plus a resize by Bob both apply.
- **Cons:** By far the most work, and every edit type needs its own logic (resize, rotate, crop, linear point editing, text). Shapes can jump under the user's cursor. Text merging is a hard problem on its own.

### D. Prevent the conflict instead (soft locks)

Broadcast "I'm resizing/editing X". Other clients block edits and deletes of X until it's released.

- **Pros:** Nothing has to be merged or cancelled, because the conflict never happens.
- **Cons:** It's the opposite of accepting incoming changes: they're blocked at the source. It also needs timeouts so locks can't get stuck.

## Recommendation

Use **A + B together**:

- **A** keeps non-conflicting changes made by others while you work, which covers most real cases.
- **B** makes deletes stick, with a clear notice instead of a silent loss or an element that comes back.
- **C** is worth considering only if users often edit the _same_ properties of one shape at the same time. That's rare in a whiteboard, and C costs much more than the others.

A + B would mean these changes:

1. **`reconcile.ts`:** for an element being edited, do a property-level merge using a table of the properties each edit controls. If the remote copy is a newer delete, return a signal saying so instead of keeping the local copy.
2. **`App`:** add `cancelInProgressEdit(elementId)`, which ends the edit on that element. For resizing it clears `resizingElement` and resets the pointer state; for text it closes the editor; for drawing it discards `newElement`. Call it when the delete signal arrives, and show a notice.
3. **Tests:**
   - a remote recolor during a resize survives, and the resize result keeps the new colour;
   - a remote delete during a resize or a text edit cancels it, and the element stays deleted on both clients;
   - both clients end up with the same element in each case.

I can implement it if you'd like.

```text
  private onKeyDownFromPointerDownHandler(
    pointerDownState: PointerDownState,
  ): (event: KeyboardEvent) => void {
    return withBatchedUpdates((event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (this.maybeHandleResize(pointerDownState, event)) {
        return;
      }
      this.maybeDragNewGenericElement(pointerDownState, event);
    });
  }

  private onKeyUpFromPointerDownHandler(
    pointerDownState: PointerDownState,
  ): (event: KeyboardEvent) => void {
    return withBatchedUpdates((event: KeyboardEvent) => {
      // Prevents focus from escaping excalidraw tab
      event.key === KEYS.ALT && event.preventDefault();
      if (this.maybeHandleResize(pointerDownState, event)) {
        return;
      }
      this.maybeDragNewGenericElement(pointerDownState, event);
    });
  }
```

```typescript
import { ShapeCache, mutateElement } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type {
  ElementsMap,
  ExcalidrawElement,
  OrderedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import type { AppState } from "../types";

/*
 * Incoming (remote) changes to an element this client is in the middle of
 * editing. The edit owns some of the element's properties (e.g. a resize owns
 * its geometry) and recomputes them on every pointer move / keystroke, so
 * remote values for those can't be taken. Everything else can:
 *
 * - properties the edit doesn't own are merged into the local element
 *   (someone recolors the shape you're resizing → both changes survive)
 * - a remote delete cancels the edit: the editor accepts the delete, stops
 *   editing and re-issues the delete (see `App.cancelInProgressEditAfterRemoteDelete`)
 *
 * Only remote changes made after the edit started (or after the last remote
 * change merged into it) are taken, so stale copies (e.g. a peer's periodic
 * full-scene broadcast) can't revert the editor's earlier changes.
 */

export type InProgressEditKind = "text" | "resize" | "new";

/** the kind of edit `elementId` is under on this client, if any */
export const getInProgressEditKind = (
  appState: Pick<
    AppState,
    "editingTextElement" | "resizingElement" | "newElement"
  >,
  elementId: string,
): InProgressEditKind | null => {
  if (appState.editingTextElement?.id === elementId) {
    return "text";
  }
  if (appState.resizingElement?.id === elementId) {
    return "resize";
  }
  if (appState.newElement?.id === elementId) {
    return "new";
  }
  return null;
};

/** the element being edited in `appState` (text edit, resize or new element) */
export const getInProgressEditElementId = (
  appState: Pick<
    AppState,
    "editingTextElement" | "resizingElement" | "newElement"
  >,
): string | null =>
  appState.editingTextElement?.id ??
  appState.resizingElement?.id ??
  appState.newElement?.id ??
  null;

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the in-progress edit's baseline (one edit per client at a time)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

type InProgressEdit = {
  elementId: string;
  /**
   * `updated` of the newest state the local element's non-edited properties
   * are known to reflect: the element's timestamp when the edit started,
   * then that of each remote change merged into it
   */
  baseUpdated: number;
  /** a remote delete was accepted: the editor must cancel the edit */
  deletedRemotely: boolean;
};

let inProgressEdit: InProgressEdit | null = null;

/** called by the editor when it starts editing `element` */
export const beginInProgressEdit = (element: ExcalidrawElement) => {
  inProgressEdit = {
    elementId: element.id,
    baseUpdated: element.updated,
    deletedRemotely: false,
  };
};

/** called by the editor when its edit ends (or is cancelled) */
export const endInProgressEdit = () => {
  inProgressEdit = null;
};

export const getInProgressEdit = (): Readonly<InProgressEdit> | null =>
  inProgressEdit;

/** whether a remote delete of the edited element was accepted */
export const isInProgressEditDeletedRemotely = (elementId: string) =>
  inProgressEdit?.elementId === elementId && inProgressEdit.deletedRemotely;

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// resolving a remote change to the element being edited
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** geometry: recomputed by resizing, rotating and drawing on every move */
const GEOMETRY_PROPS = [
  "x",
  "y",
  "width",
  "height",
  "angle",
  "points",
  "pressures",
  "scale",
  "crop",
  "lastCommittedPoint",
  "startBinding",
  "endBinding",
  "fixedSegments",
  "startIsSpecial",
  "endIsSpecial",
  // text resizes scale the font and re-wrap the text
  "fontSize",
  "lineHeight",
  "text",
  "autoResize",
];

/** properties each kind of edit owns (remote values for them are dropped) */
const EDIT_OWNED_PROPS: Record<InProgressEditKind, ReadonlySet<string>> = {
  resize: new Set(GEOMETRY_PROPS),
  new: new Set(GEOMETRY_PROPS),
  // typing changes the text and, through it, the dimensions / position
  text: new Set([
    ...GEOMETRY_PROPS,
    "originalText",
    "textHyperlinks",
    "verticalAlign",
    "textAlign",
  ]),
};

/** never taken from a remote copy while editing */
const NEVER_MERGED_PROPS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "id",
  "type",
  "version",
  "versionNonce",
  "updated",
  "seed",
  // deletion is handled separately (it cancels the edit)
  "isDeleted",
  // co-owners are merged by `mergeCoOwnership`, the rest is host data
  "customData",
]);

const isSameValue = (a: unknown, b: unknown) =>
  a === b ||
  (typeof a === "object" &&
    typeof b === "object" &&
    a !== null &&
    b !== null &&
    JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b));

const isValidTimestamp = (timestamp: unknown): timestamp is number =>
  typeof timestamp === "number" && Number.isFinite(timestamp);

/**
 * The remote properties to merge into `local` (those the edit doesn't own
 * and that differ).
 */
export const getMergeableRemoteChanges = (
  local: ExcalidrawElement,
  remote: ExcalidrawElement,
  kind: InProgressEditKind,
): Partial<ExcalidrawElement> => {
  const owned = EDIT_OWNED_PROPS[kind];
  const updates: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(remote)) {
    if (
      !NEVER_MERGED_PROPS.has(key) &&
      !owned.has(key) &&
      !isSameValue(
        local[key as keyof ExcalidrawElement],
        remote[key as keyof ExcalidrawElement],
      )
    ) {
      updates[key] = remote[key as keyof ExcalidrawElement];
    }
  }
  return updates as Partial<ExcalidrawElement>;
};

/**
 * Resolves a remote copy of an element this client is editing:
 *
 * - `"acceptRemote"`: it's a delete made after the edit started. The caller
 *   takes the remote (deleted) copy, and the editor cancels the edit.
 * - `"keepLocal"`: the edit keeps the local copy. Remote changes made after
 *   the edit started, to properties the edit doesn't own, have been merged
 *   into it (in place, bumping its version so they're re-broadcast).
 *
 * Without a registered baseline for the edit (a host that doesn't call
 * `beginInProgressEdit`), the local copy is kept as is.
 */
export const resolveRemoteChangeToInProgressEdit = (
  local: OrderedExcalidrawElement,
  remote: OrderedExcalidrawElement,
  kind: InProgressEditKind,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): "acceptRemote" | "keepLocal" => {
  const edit = inProgressEdit;
  if (
    !edit ||
    edit.elementId !== local.id ||
    !isValidTimestamp(remote.updated) ||
    remote.updated <= edit.baseUpdated
  ) {
    return "keepLocal";
  }

  if (remote.isDeleted && !local.isDeleted) {
    edit.deletedRemotely = true;
    return "acceptRemote";
  }

  const updates = getMergeableRemoteChanges(local, remote, kind);
  if (Object.keys(updates).length) {
    mutateElement(local, elementsMap, updates);
    // the cached shape is keyed by element object and wouldn't notice
    // style changes made in place
    ShapeCache.delete(local);
  }
  edit.baseUpdated = remote.updated;
  return "keepLocal";
};
```

```bash
   * Keeps the in-progress edit's baseline (see inProgressEdit.ts) in sync
   * with the edit state, and cancels the edit once a collaborator's delete
   * of the element was accepted.
   */
  private syncInProgressEdit() {
    const elementId = getInProgressEditElementId(this.state);

    if (elementId && isInProgressEditDeletedRemotely(elementId)) {
      this.cancelInProgressEditAfterRemoteDelete(elementId);
      return;
    }

    if (elementId !== (getInProgressEdit()?.elementId ?? null)) {
      const element = elementId && this.scene.getElement(elementId);
      if (element) {
        beginInProgressEdit(element);
      } else {
        endInProgressEdit();
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * A collaborator deleted the element this client is editing: stop the edit
   * without applying it, and re-issue the delete with a new timestamp, so it
   * also wins against changes this client broadcast before the delete
   * arrived (which may have restored the element on other clients).
   */
  private cancelInProgressEditAfterRemoteDelete(elementId: string) {
    endInProgressEdit();

    // text editing: close the editor without writing back
    if (this.textEditor) {
      this.textEditor.cancel();
      this.textEditor = null;
```

```text
import { waitFor } from "@testing-library/dom";
import { fireEvent } from "@testing-library/react";

import {
  stripIgnoredNodesFromErrorMessage,
  trimErrorStack,
} from "../test-utils";

export const TEXT_EDITOR_SELECTOR =
  ".excalidraw-textEditorContainer > textarea";

export const getTextEditor = async ({
  selector = TEXT_EDITOR_SELECTOR,
  waitForEditor = true,
}: { selector?: string; waitForEditor?: boolean } = {}) => {
  const error = trimErrorStack(new Error());
  try {
    const query = () => document.querySelector(selector) as HTMLTextAreaElement;
    if (waitForEditor) {
      await waitFor(() => expect(query()).not.toBe(null));
      return query();
    }
    return query();
  } catch (err: any) {
    stripIgnoredNodesFromErrorMessage(err);
    err.stack = error.stack;
    throw err;
  }
};

export const updateTextEditor = (
  editor: HTMLTextAreaElement | HTMLInputElement,
  value: string,
) => {
  fireEvent.change(editor, { target: { value } });
  fireEvent.input(editor);
};
```

```text
export class Pointer {
  public clientX = 0;
  public clientY = 0;

  static activePointers: Pointer[] = [];
  static resetAll() {
    Pointer.activePointers.forEach((pointer) => pointer.reset());
  }

  constructor(
    private readonly pointerType: "mouse" | "touch" | "pen",
    private readonly pointerId = 1,
  ) {
    Pointer.activePointers.push(this);
  }

  reset() {
    this.clientX = 0;
    this.clientY = 0;
  // incremental (moving by deltas)
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  move(dx: number, dy: number) {
    if (dx !== 0 || dy !== 0) {
      this.clientX += dx;
      this.clientY += dy;
      fireEvent.pointerMove(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, this.getEvent());
    }
  }

  down(dx = 0, dy = 0) {
    this.move(dx, dy);
    fireEvent.pointerDown(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, this.getEvent());
  }

  up(dx = 0, dy = 0) {
    this.move(dx, dy);
    fireEvent.pointerUp(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, this.getEvent());
  }

  click(dx = 0, dy = 0) {
    this.down(dx, dy);
    this.up();
  }

  doubleClick(dx = 0, dy = 0) {
    this.move(dx, dy);
    fireEvent.doubleClick(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, this.getEvent());
  }

  // absolute coords
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  moveTo(x: number = this.clientX, y: number = this.clientY) {
    this.clientX = x;
    this.clientY = y;
    // fire "mousemove" to update editor cursor position
    fireEvent.mouseMove(document, this.getEvent());
    fireEvent.pointerMove(GlobalTestState.interactiveCanvas, this.getEvent());

    this.clientY = y;
```

```typescript
/**
 * Remote changes to an element this client is editing (resizing, text
 * editing): properties the edit doesn't own are merged in, and a remote
 * delete cancels the edit (and is re-issued so it sticks).
 */
import { KEYS, arrayToMap } from "@excalidraw/common";
import { CaptureUpdateAction, getTransformHandles } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type {
  ExcalidrawElement,
  OrderedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";
import {
  endInProgressEdit,
  getInProgressEdit,
  getMergeableRemoteChanges,
} from "../data/inProgressEdit";
import { reconcileElements } from "../data/reconcile";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Keyboard, Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";
import { getTextEditor, TEXT_EDITOR_SELECTOR } from "./queries/dom";
import { act, fireEvent, render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

import type { RemoteExcalidrawElement } from "../data/reconcile";

unmountComponent();

const h = window.h;
const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

const get = (id: string) =>
  h.app.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted().find((el) => el.id === id)!;

/**
 * A collaborator's copy of the element: `changes` applied on top of what we
 * have, made at `updated` (test elements are all stamped `updated: 1`, so
 * anything later counts as made after the edit started).
 */
const remoteCopy = (
  id: string,
  changes: Partial<ExcalidrawElement>,
  updated = 1000,
) =>
  ({
    ...get(id),
    ...changes,
    version: get(id).version + 1,
    versionNonce: 42,
    updated,
  } as RemoteExcalidrawElement);

/** applies a remote update the way collaboration does */
const receive = (remote: RemoteExcalidrawElement) => {
  act(() => {
    h.app.updateScene({
      elements: reconcileElements(
        h.app.scene.getElementsIncludingDeleted() as OrderedExcalidrawElement[],
        [remote],
        h.state,
      ),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });
  });
};

/** starts resizing `id` from its south-east handle, mid-gesture */
const startResize = (id: string) => {
  API.setSelectedElements([get(id)]);
  const [x, y, w, hgt] = getTransformHandles(
    get(id),
    h.state.zoom,
    arrayToMap(h.elements),
    "mouse",
    {},
  ).se!;
  mouse.reset();
  mouse.down(x + w / 2, y + hgt / 2);
  mouse.move(20, 20);
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  endInProgressEdit();
  await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  API.setElements([
    API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      id: "rect",
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      strokeColor: "#000000",
    }),
    API.createElement({
      type: "text",
      id: "text",
      x: 300,
      y: 0,
      text: "hello",
      strokeColor: "#000000",
    }),
  ]);
});

describe("getMergeableRemoteChanges", () => {
  it("takes style changes but not what a resize owns", () => {
    const local = API.createElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, width: 50 });
    const remote = {
      ...local,
      x: 99,
      width: 10,
      strokeColor: "#ff0000",
      opacity: 40,
      version: 99,
      updated: 1000,
      isDeleted: true,
      customData: { creatorId: "x" },
    };
    expect(getMergeableRemoteChanges(local, remote, "resize")).toEqual({
      strokeColor: "#ff0000",
      opacity: 40,
    });
  });

  it("a text edit owns the text but not its color", () => {
    const local = API.createElement({ type: "text", text: "a" });
    const remote = {
      ...local,
      text: "b",
      originalText: "b",
      strokeColor: "red",
    };
    expect(getMergeableRemoteChanges(local, remote, "text")).toEqual({
      strokeColor: "red",
    });
  });
});

describe("while resizing", () => {
  it("tracks the edit's baseline from the element's pre-edit timestamp", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    expect(h.state.resizingElement?.id).toBe("rect");
    expect(getInProgressEdit()).toEqual({
      elementId: "rect",
      baseUpdated: 1,
      deletedRemotely: false,
    });
    mouse.up();
    expect(getInProgressEdit()).toBeNull();
  });

  it("a remote recolor is merged; remote geometry is not", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    receive(remoteCopy("rect", { strokeColor: "#ff0000", x: 500 }));

    expect(h.state.resizingElement?.id).toBe("rect");
    expect(get("rect").strokeColor).toBe("#ff0000");
    expect(get("rect").x).toBe(0);

    mouse.move(10, 10);
    mouse.up();
    expect(get("rect").strokeColor).toBe("#ff0000");
    expect(get("rect").width).toBe(130);
    expect(get("rect").x).toBe(0);
  });

  it("a stale remote copy (from before the edit) is ignored", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    receive(remoteCopy("rect", { strokeColor: "#ff0000" }, 1));
    expect(get("rect").strokeColor).toBe("#000000");
    mouse.up();
  });

  it("after merging a change, an older remote copy can't revert it", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    receive(remoteCopy("rect", { strokeColor: "#ff0000" }, 1000));
    receive(remoteCopy("rect", { strokeColor: "#00ff00" }, 500));
    expect(get("rect").strokeColor).toBe("#ff0000");
    mouse.up();
  });

  it("a remote delete cancels the resize, and the element stays deleted", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    const widthBefore = get("rect").width;
    receive(remoteCopy("rect", { isDeleted: true }));

    expect(h.state.resizingElement).toBeNull();
    expect(h.state.isResizing).toBe(false);
    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds.rect).toBeUndefined();
    expect(h.state.toast?.message).toMatch(/deleted the element/);
    expect(get("rect").isDeleted).toBe(true);
    expect(getInProgressEdit()).toBeNull();

    // the rest of the gesture does nothing
    mouse.move(50, 50);
    mouse.up();
    expect(get("rect").isDeleted).toBe(true);
    expect(get("rect").width).toBe(widthBefore);
  });

  it("the delete is re-issued as a newer change than the remote one", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    const remote = remoteCopy("rect", { isDeleted: true });
    receive(remote);
    expect(get("rect").version).toBeGreaterThan(remote.version);
    mouse.up();
  });

  it("a stale remote delete (from before the edit) doesn't cancel it", () => {
    startResize("rect");
    receive(remoteCopy("rect", { isDeleted: true }, 1));
    expect(h.state.resizingElement?.id).toBe("rect");
    expect(get("rect").isDeleted).toBe(false);
    mouse.up();
  });
});

describe("while editing text", () => {
  const openEditor = async () => {
    API.setSelectedElements([get("text")]);
    Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER);
    const editor = await getTextEditor();
    expect(h.state.editingTextElement?.id).toBe("text");
    return editor;
  };

  it("a remote recolor is merged; the remote text is not", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor();
    fireEvent.input(editor, { target: { value: "mine" } });

    receive(
      remoteCopy("text", {
        strokeColor: "#ff0000",
        text: "theirs",
        originalText: "theirs",
      } as Partial<ExcalidrawElement>),
    );
    expect(get("text").strokeColor).toBe("#ff0000");

    act(() => editor.blur());
    expect((get("text") as any).originalText).toBe("mine");
    expect(get("text").strokeColor).toBe("#ff0000");
  });

  it("a remote delete closes the editor without writing the text back", async () => {
    const editor = await openEditor();
    fireEvent.input(editor, { target: { value: "unsaved" } });

    receive(remoteCopy("text", { isDeleted: true }));

    expect(h.state.editingTextElement).toBeNull();
    expect(document.querySelector(TEXT_EDITOR_SELECTOR)).toBeNull();
    expect(get("text").isDeleted).toBe(true);
    expect(h.state.toast?.message).toMatch(/deleted the element/);

    // a late blur can't resurrect it
    act(() => editor.blur());
    expect(get("text").isDeleted).toBe(true);
  });
});
```
