_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 02:47:44Z)**_

No. Deletes now stick in far more cases, but a few situations can still bring an element back.

## Cases that now stay deleted

- **Resizing, text editing, or drawing it:** the delete cancels the edit, and the editor's client issues the delete again with a later timestamp.
  - If the editor had already broadcast a change made after the delete, other clients may briefly show the element again. The re-issued delete then removes it for everyone.
- **Editing it before the delete happened:** the delete is the later change, so it wins.
- **Merely having it selected:** the delete wins.

## Cases where it can come back

1. **Undo.** Anyone who undoes the delete, or undoes their own earlier edit, creates a newer change and restores the element. This is intended.

2. **Edits not covered by A+B.** The cancel-on-delete behaviour only covers the three protected edits: resizing a single element, text editing, and drawing a new element. These follow the plain "latest change wins" rule instead:

   - dragging
   - resizing or rotating several elements at once
   - editing points on lines and arrows
   - cropping
   - arrow-key nudges

   So if Bob is still dragging when Alice's delete reaches him, his next move is newer than the delete. The element comes back for everyone.

3. **Side effects on another client.** Bob moves a shape at about the same time Alice deletes an arrow attached to it. Bob's client reroutes the arrow with a later timestamp and brings it back. This only happens if the two actions overlap; once Bob has received the delete, deleted arrows aren't updated.

4. **The editor disconnects at the wrong moment.** Bob is resizing, broadcasts a move made after the delete, then loses connection before receiving it. His move brings the element back on other clients, and he never re-issues the delete.

5. **Clock skew before the first exchange.** If Alice's device clock is behind and the two clients haven't exchanged any changes yet, her delete can look older than it is. There are two ways this goes wrong:

   - It loses to a concurrent edit.
   - During a protected edit, it can even be treated as a stale copy and ignored.

   After the first exchange the clocks line up, and how far ahead a remote timestamp can push a clock is capped at 60 seconds.

6. **Old copies after 24 hours.** The web app stops syncing deleted elements 24 hours after deletion (`DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT` in `excalidraw-app/app_constants.ts`). A tab that was offline longer than that and still holds the element can bring it back when it reconnects, because nobody has the deletion any more.

## Closing the remaining gaps

- **Cases 2–4:** extend the same treatment to dragging and the other uncovered edits. Their state lives in `pointerDownState`, and the gesture-cancel code I added would work for them. Alternatively, let a remote delete always win against changes that started _before_ the delete arrived.
- **Case 5:** add a logical counter to the clock (a full hybrid logical clock), which also orders events correctly between clients that haven't exchanged any changes yet.
- **Case 6:** keep deletions longer, or refuse to bring back elements whose deletion has expired.

Dragging (case 2) is the one users are most likely to run into. I can extend A+B to cover it if you'd like.

The full check for the A+B change is still running in the background. I'll report its result when it finishes.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-13 02:57:11Z)**_

Yes, it's worth extending, but for a different reason than protection. Uncovered edits aren't protected, so incoming changes _can_ be accepted during them. In practice they almost never are, because the local copy keeps winning on timestamp.

## Why "not protected" doesn't mean "accepted"

An incoming change is accepted only if it's newer than the local copy. During a drag, Bob's client re-stamps the element on every pointer move, many times a second. Say Alice recolors at time T:

1. Her change reaches Bob roughly 50–150 ms later, at T + latency.
2. Bob has moved the shape several times in between, so his local copy is newer than T.
3. Her recolor is discarded as stale, and Bob's next broadcast puts the old colour back on everyone's screen.

A delete fails the same way: Bob's newer moves win, and the element comes back. So during any continuous edit, the result is the same as the old protection: incoming changes are dropped. Only changes that arrive while Bob is holding still get through.

## What happens to an accepted change mid-drag

Accepting one is already safe. Dragging computes each position from the copy taken when the drag started (`pointerDownState.originalElements`, `dragElements.ts:107`) and only writes `x`/`y`. A recolor accepted mid-drag would survive, and the drag would keep working. Nothing needs to be rebuilt; the change only needs to win the comparison.

## Which edits are affected

| Edit | Continuous? | Remote changes lost during it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dragging | Yes | Almost always |
| Resizing or rotating several elements | Yes | Almost always |
| Editing points on lines and arrows | Yes | Almost always |
| Cropping | Yes | Almost always |
| Arrow-key nudge, property-panel change | No, one event | Only if both changes land within the network delay. That's a true simultaneous edit, which latest-change-wins handles correctly. |

## Two ways to fix it

1. **Give each continuous edit the same treatment as A+B.** Each edit gets a list of properties it owns; for example, a drag owns `x`/`y` (and `frameId` if it moves the element into a frame). Merge everything else from newer remote copies, measured from when the edit started, and let a newer delete cancel the edit.

   - **Pros:** Reuses the code already written (`inProgressEdit.ts`, the start-of-edit baseline, the gesture cancel).
   - **Cons:** Each edit must report which element(s) it's working on. A drag or a multi-element transform covers several elements, so the registry would need to track a set instead of one element. Every new kind of edit has to be added by hand.

2. **Make the merge general.** Track which properties each element last changed locally and when (relative to the last remote copy seen). Merge per property for any element, edited or not.
   - **Pros:** Covers every edit, including side effects like arrows rerouted by a moved shape, with no per-edit lists.
   - **Cons:** This is the larger per-property merge option. It needs extra bookkeeping on every local change, and it replaces A+B rather than building on it.

## Recommendation

Do option 1 for dragging and multi-element transforms. Those are the edits where users will notice lost recolours and deletes that come back, and they reuse almost all of the A+B code. The main change is letting the registry hold several element ids. Point editing and cropping can follow the same pattern later if needed.

```bash
import { ShapeCache, mutateElement } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type {
  ElementsMap,
  ExcalidrawElement,
  OrderedExcalidrawElement,
} from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import type { AppState } from "../types";

/*
 * Incoming (remote) changes to elements this client is in the middle of
 * editing. An edit owns some of an element's properties (e.g. a resize owns
 * its geometry) and recomputes them on every pointer move / keystroke, and
 * the edited elements' timestamps keep advancing while it does, so without
 * special handling remote changes made meanwhile would be lost. Instead:
 *
 * - properties the edit doesn't own are merged into the local element
 *   (someone recolors the shape you're dragging → both changes survive)
 * - a remote delete is accepted: a drag carries on without the element;
 *   other edits are cancelled. The editor re-issues the delete (see
 *   `App.handleRemoteDeletesOfInProgressEdit`).
 *
 * Only remote changes made after the edit started (or after the last remote
 * change merged into that element) are taken, so stale copies (e.g. a peer's
 * periodic full-scene broadcast) can't revert the editor's earlier changes.
 */

export type InProgressEditKind =
  /** typing in a text element or label */
  | "text"
  /** resizing / rotating a single element */
  | "resize"
  /** drawing a new element */
  | "new"
  /** dragging the selection */
  | "drag"
  /** resizing / rotating several elements at once */
  | "transform";

type ProtectedEditState = Pick<
  AppState,
  "editingTextElement" | "resizingElement" | "newElement"
>;

/**
 * Edits whose local copy always wins over the usual "latest change wins"
 * rule (they hold references to the element, or rebuild it from local
 * state). Dragging and multi-element transforms aren't protected that way:
 * they only get the merge below, when registered.
 */
export const getProtectedEditKind = (
  appState: ProtectedEditState,
  elementId: string,
): "text" | "resize" | "new" | null => {
  if (appState.editingTextElement?.id === elementId) {
    return "text";
  }
  if (appState.resizingElement?.id === elementId) {
    return "resize";
  }
  if (appState.newElement?.id === elementId) {
    return "new";
  }
  return null;
};

/** the kind of in-progress edit `elementId` is part of on this client */
export const getInProgressEditKind = (
  appState: ProtectedEditState,
  elementId: string,
): InProgressEditKind | null =>
  getProtectedEditKind(appState, elementId) ??
  (inProgressEdit?.bases.has(elementId) ? inProgressEdit.kind : null);

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// the in-progress edit's baselines (one edit per client at a time)
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

type InProgressEdit = {
  kind: InProgressEditKind;
  /**
   * per edited element, `updated` of the newest state its non-edited
   * properties are known to reflect: the element's timestamp when the edit
   * started, then that of each remote change merged into it
   */
  bases: Map<string, number>;
  /** elements whose remote delete was accepted (the editor must react) */
  deletedRemotely: Set<string>;
};

let inProgressEdit: InProgressEdit | null = null;

/**
 * Called by the editor when an edit starts.
 *
 * @param elements the edited elements as they were when the edit started
 */
export const beginInProgressEdit = (
  kind: InProgressEditKind,
  elements: Iterable<Pick<ExcalidrawElement, "id" | "updated">>,
) => {
  const bases = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const element of elements) {
    bases.set(element.id, element.updated);
  }
  inProgressEdit = { kind, bases, deletedRemotely: new Set() };
};

/** called by the editor when its edit ends (or is cancelled) */
export const endInProgressEdit = () => {
  inProgressEdit = null;
};

export const getInProgressEdit = (): Readonly<InProgressEdit> | null =>
  inProgressEdit;

/**
 * Returns the edited elements whose remote delete was accepted since the
 * last call (and forgets them).
 */
export const takeRemotelyDeletedEditElements = (): string[] => {
  if (!inProgressEdit?.deletedRemotely.size) {
    return [];
  }
  const ids = [...inProgressEdit.deletedRemotely];
  inProgressEdit.deletedRemotely.clear();
  for (const id of ids) {
    inProgressEdit.bases.delete(id);
  }
  return ids;
};

EOF
```

```text
const EDIT_OWNED_PROPS: Record<InProgressEditKind, ReadonlySet<string>> = {
  resize: new Set(GEOMETRY_PROPS),
  new: new Set(GEOMETRY_PROPS),
  // typing changes the text and, through it, the dimensions / position
  text: new Set([
    ...GEOMETRY_PROPS,
    "originalText",
    "textHyperlinks",
    "verticalAlign",
    "textAlign",
  ]),
};

/** never taken from a remote copy while editing */
const NEVER_MERGED_PROPS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "id",
};

/**
 * Resolves a remote copy of an element this client is editing:
 *
 * - `"acceptRemote"`: it's a delete made after the edit started. The caller
 *   takes the remote (deleted) copy, and the editor cancels the edit.
 * - `"keepLocal"`: the edit keeps the local copy. Remote changes made after
 *   the edit started, to properties the edit doesn't own, have been merged
 *   into it (in place, bumping its version so they're re-broadcast).
 *
 * Without a registered baseline for the edit (a host that doesn't call
 * `beginInProgressEdit`), the local copy is kept as is.
 */
export const resolveRemoteChangeToInProgressEdit = (
  local: OrderedExcalidrawElement,
  remote: OrderedExcalidrawElement,
  kind: InProgressEditKind,
  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
): "acceptRemote" | "keepLocal" => {
  const edit = inProgressEdit;
  if (
    !edit ||
    edit.elementId !== local.id ||
    !isValidTimestamp(remote.updated) ||
    remote.updated <= edit.baseUpdated
  ) {
    return "keepLocal";
  }

  if (remote.isDeleted && !local.isDeleted) {
    edit.deletedRemotely = true;
    return "acceptRemote";
  }

  const updates = getMergeableRemoteChanges(local, remote, kind);
  if (Object.keys(updates).length) {
    mutateElement(
      local,
      elementsMap,
      updates as Parameters<typeof mutateElement>[2],
    );
    // the cached shape is keyed by element object and wouldn't notice
    // style changes made in place
    ShapeCache.delete(local);
  }
  edit.baseUpdated = remote.updated;
  return "keepLocal";
};
```

```bash
  /** the kind of edit in progress on this client, if any */
  private getCurrentEditKind(): InProgressEditKind | null {
    const { state } = this;
    if (state.editingTextElement) {
      return "text";
    }
    if (state.resizingElement) {
      return "resize";
    }
    if (state.newElement) {
      return "new";
    }
    if (state.selectedElementsAreBeingDragged) {
      return "drag";
    }
    if (state.isResizing || state.isRotating) {
      return "transform";
    }
    return null;
  }

  /**
   * The elements an edit changes: the edited element, or for a drag /
   * multi-element transform the selection with its labels and frame
   * children, plus the arrows rerouted because they're bound to it.
   */
  private getEditedElementIds(kind: InProgressEditKind): Set<string> {
    const { state } = this;
    if (kind === "text" || kind === "resize" || kind === "new") {
      const element =
        kind === "text"
          ? state.editingTextElement
          : kind === "resize"
          ? state.resizingElement
          : state.newElement;
      return new Set(element ? [element.id] : []);
    }

    const ids = new Set<string>();
    for (const element of this.scene.getSelectedElements({
      selectedElementIds: state.selectedElementIds,
      includeBoundTextElement: true,
      includeElementsInFrames: true,
    })) {
      ids.add(element.id);
      for (const bound of element.boundElements ?? []) {
        ids.add(bound.id);
      }
    }
    return ids;
  }

  /**
   * Keeps the in-progress edit's baselines (see inProgressEdit.ts) in sync
   * with the edit state, and reacts to collaborators' deletes of edited
   * elements once they were accepted.
   */
  private syncInProgressEdit() {
    const deletedIds = takeRemotelyDeletedEditElements();
    if (deletedIds.length) {
      this.handleRemoteDeletesOfInProgressEdit(deletedIds);
    }

    const kind = this.getCurrentEditKind();
    const edit = getInProgressEdit();
    if (kind === (edit?.kind ?? null)) {
      return;
    }
    if (!kind) {
      endInProgressEdit();
      return;
    }

    // baselines from before the gesture started when we have them (the
    // first move may already have changed the elements)
    const originals = this.activePointerDownState?.originalElements;
    const elements = [];
    for (const id of this.getEditedElementIds(kind)) {
      const element = originals?.get(id) ?? this.scene.getElement(id);
      if (element) {
        elements.push(element);
      }
    }
    beginInProgressEdit(kind, elements);
  }

  /**
   * Collaborators deleted elements this client is editing. A drag carries on
   * without them; any other edit is stopped without being applied. Either
   * way the delete is re-issued with a new timestamp, so it also wins against
   * changes this client broadcast before the delete arrived (which may have
   * restored the element on other clients).
   */
  private handleRemoteDeletesOfInProgressEdit(elementIds: readonly string[]) {
    const deleted = new Set(elementIds);

    if (this.getCurrentEditKind() !== "drag") {
      this.cancelInProgressEdit();
    }

    // re-issue the deletes
    this.updateScene({
      elements: this.scene
        .getElementsIncludingDeleted()
        .map((el) =>
          deleted.has(el.id) ? newElementWith(el, { isDeleted: true }, true) : el,
        ),
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });

    this.setState((prevState) => ({
      selectedElementIds: Object.keys(prevState.selectedElementIds).some((id) =>
        deleted.has(id),
      )
        ? makeNextSelectedElementIds(
            Object.fromEntries(
              Object.keys(prevState.selectedElementIds)
                .filter((id) => !deleted.has(id))
                .map((id) => [id, true as const]),
            ),
            prevState,
          )
        : prevState.selectedElementIds,
      multiElement:
        prevState.multiElement && deleted.has(prevState.multiElement.id)
          ? null
          : prevState.multiElement,
      selectedLinearElement:
        prevState.selectedLinearElement &&
        deleted.has(prevState.selectedLinearElement.elementId)
          ? null
          : prevState.selectedLinearElement,
      toast: {
        message: t("collaboratorEdit.deletedWhileEditing"),
        duration: 5000,
      },
    }));
  }

  /**
   * Stops the edit in progress without applying the rest of it: closes the
   * text editor without writing back, or drops the pointer gesture's
   * listeners without finishing it.
   */
  private cancelInProgressEdit() {
    endInProgressEdit();

    if (this.textEditor) {
      this.textEditor.cancel();
      this.textEditor = null;
    }

    const pointerDownState = this.activePointerDownState;
    if (pointerDownState) {
      this.activePointerDownState = null;
      this.missingPointerEventCleanupEmitter.clear();
      const { onMove, onUp, onKeyDown, onKeyUp } =
        pointerDownState.eventListeners;
      onMove?.cancel();
      onMove && window.removeEventListener(EVENT.POINTER_MOVE, onMove);
      onUp && window.removeEventListener(EVENT.POINTER_UP, onUp);
      onKeyDown && window.removeEventListener(EVENT.KEYDOWN, onKeyDown);
      onKeyUp && window.removeEventListener(EVENT.KEYUP, onKeyUp);
      this.lassoTrail.endPath();
      this.previousPointerMoveCoords = null;
      SnapCache.setReferenceSnapPoints(null);
      SnapCache.setVisibleGaps(null);
    }

    this.setState((prevState) => ({
      editingTextElement: null,
      newElement: null,
      resizingElement: null,
      isResizing: false,
      isRotating: false,
      selectedElementsAreBeingDragged: false,
      selectionElement: null,
      cursorButton: "up",
      snapLines: updateStable(prevState.snapLines, []),
      originSnapOffset: null,
    }));
    this.focusContainer();
  }
```

```typescript
/**
 * Hybrid logical clock (HLC) for element `updated` timestamps, which
 * collaboration uses to decide which concurrent copy of an element wins
 * ("the latest change wins", see `reconcileElements`).
 *
 * A timestamp is (physical ms, logical counter), encoded in one number as
 * `ms + counter / 1024` so the element format doesn't change: older clients
 * and other code (e.g. expiring deleted elements) still read it as a ms
 * timestamp. Up to 2^43 ms (year ~2248) the encoding is exact in a double.
 *
 * - it follows the wall clock, and never goes backwards even if the device
 *   clock does
 * - every local change gets a timestamp strictly greater than any timestamp
 *   this clock returned or observed before: a change made after seeing
 *   another client's change is always newer than it, even when both happen
 *   in the same millisecond or this device's clock is behind
 * - remote timestamps too far ahead of the local wall clock are only adopted
 *   up to `maxDriftMs`, so one client with a badly wrong clock can't drag
 *   everyone's clock forward
 *
 * What no clock can do: order changes made *concurrently* on devices whose
 * clocks disagree, before they've exchanged anything. Those are ordered by
 * their (skewed) wall clocks.
 */

/** logical ticks per ms */
export const HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION = 1024;

const MAX_COUNTER = HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION - 1;

/** splits an encoded timestamp into its physical ms and logical counter */
export const decodeHybridTimestamp = (
  timestamp: number,
): [physical: number, counter: number] => {
  const physical = Math.floor(timestamp);
  const counter = Math.min(
    MAX_COUNTER,
    Math.round((timestamp - physical) * HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION),
  );
  return [physical, counter];
};

export const encodeHybridTimestamp = (physical: number, counter: number) =>
  physical + counter / HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION;

export class HybridClock {
  private physical = 0;
  private counter = 0;

  constructor(
    private readonly now: () => number = Date.now,
    private readonly maxDriftMs = 60 * 1000,
  ) {}

  /** a timestamp for a local change: greater than any returned/observed */
  tick(): number {
    const wallClock = Math.floor(this.now());
    if (wallClock > this.physical) {
      this.physical = wallClock;
      this.counter = 0;
    } else if (this.counter < MAX_COUNTER) {
      this.counter++;
    } else {
      // more than 1024 changes within one ms: borrow the next ms
      this.physical++;
      this.counter = 0;
    }
    return encodeHybridTimestamp(this.physical, this.counter);
  }

  /** advances the clock to a timestamp seen on a remote element */
  observe(timestamp: unknown) {
    if (typeof timestamp !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(timestamp)) {
      return;
    }
    const maxAdoptable = Math.floor(this.now()) + this.maxDriftMs;
    const [physical, counter] =
      timestamp > maxAdoptable
        ? [maxAdoptable, 0]
        : decodeHybridTimestamp(timestamp);

    if (
      physical > this.physical ||
      (physical === this.physical && counter > this.counter)
    ) {
      this.physical = physical;
      this.counter = counter;
    }
  }
}

/** the editor's clock for element `updated` timestamps */
export const elementClock = new HybridClock();
```

```bash
describe("HybridClock", () => {
  const parts = (timestamp: number) => decodeHybridTimestamp(timestamp);

  it("follows the wall clock", () => {
    let now = 1000;
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => now);
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1000);
    now = 1500;
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1500);
  });

  it("changes within the same ms get increasing logical counters", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    const a = clock.tick();
    const b = clock.tick();
    const c = clock.tick();
    expect([a, b, c].map(parts)).toEqual([
      [1000, 0],
      [1000, 1],
      [1000, 2],
    ]);
    expect(a < b && b < c).toBe(true);
  });

  it("never goes backwards, even if the device clock does", () => {
    let now = 1000;
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => now);
    const before = clock.tick();
    now = 400;
    const after = clock.tick();
    expect(after).toBeGreaterThan(before);
    expect(parts(after)).toEqual([1000, 1]);
  });

  it("a change after observing a remote one is strictly newer (device clock behind)", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    clock.observe(5000);
    expect(clock.tick()).toBeGreaterThan(5000);
    expect(parts(clock.tick())).toEqual([5000, 2]);
  });

  it("a change after observing a remote one in the same ms is strictly newer", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    const remote = encodeHybridTimestamp(1000, 7);
    clock.observe(remote);
    expect(clock.tick()).toBeGreaterThan(remote);
    expect(parts(clock.tick())).toEqual([1000, 9]);
  });

  it("ignores observed timestamps older than its own", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    clock.tick();
    clock.observe(10);
    expect(parts(clock.tick())).toEqual([1000, 1]);
  });

  it("adopts remote timestamps only up to the max drift ahead of the wall clock", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000, 60_000);
    clock.observe(1000 + 3_600_000);
    expect(parts(clock.tick())).toEqual([61_000, 1]);
  });

  it("borrows the next ms after 1024 changes within one ms", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    let last = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION; i++) {
      last = clock.tick();
    }
    expect(parts(last)).toEqual([1000, HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION - 1]);
    const next = clock.tick();
    expect(next).toBeGreaterThan(last);
    expect(parts(next)).toEqual([1001, 0]);
  });

  it("encodes exactly for present-day timestamps", () => {
    const physical = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 12);
    for (const counter of [0, 1, 511, HLC_COUNTER_RESOLUTION - 1]) {
      expect(parts(encodeHybridTimestamp(physical, counter))).toEqual([
        physical,
        counter,
      ]);
    }
  });

  it("ignores invalid timestamps", () => {
    const clock = new HybridClock(() => 1000);
    clock.observe(undefined);
    clock.observe(NaN);
    clock.observe(Infinity);
    clock.observe("9999");
    expect(clock.tick()).toBe(1000);
  });
});
```

```typescript
import { DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT } from "../app_constants";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

/*
 * Deleted elements are only synced for `DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT` (see
 * `isSyncableElement`). After that, the room forgets the deletion, so a
 * client that kept a live copy all along (e.g. a tab offline for longer)
 * would bring the element back when it syncs again.
 *
 * The rule that catches it: a live element is synced within seconds of every
 * change, so a live element whose last change is older than the deletion
 * timeout is always part of the room's scene. If the room's scene doesn't
 * have it, it was deleted and that deletion has since expired.
 */

/** whether the element's last change is older than the deletion timeout */
export const isPastDeletionExpiry = (
  element: Pick<ExcalidrawElement, "updated">,
  now = Date.now(),
) =>
  typeof element.updated === "number" &&
  element.updated < now - DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT;

/**
 * Receiving side: ids of remote elements to ignore, i.e. live elements this
 * client doesn't have (its scene came from the room's) that haven't changed
 * since before the deletion timeout.
 *
 * Only for incremental updates. Not for the room scene a client starts from
 * (everything in it is new to the client) or the room's stored scene (it's
 * the reference for what the room has).
 */
export const getExpiredResurrections = (
  remoteElements: readonly ExcalidrawElement[],
  localElementsMap: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>,
  now = Date.now(),
): Set<string> => {
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  for (const element of remoteElements) {
    if (
      !element.isDeleted &&
      !localElementsMap.has(element.id) &&
      isPastDeletionExpiry(element, now)
    ) {
      ids.add(element.id);
    }
  }
  return ids;
};

/**
 * Sending side: local live elements whose deletion expired, i.e. the room's
 * full scene doesn't have them, this client synced them with the room
 * before, and they haven't changed since before the deletion timeout.
 *
 * Elements this client never synced (e.g. drawn while offline) are kept: the
 * room can't have seen them.
 */
export const getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion = <
  T extends ExcalidrawElement,
>(
  localElements: readonly T[],
  roomElementIds: ReadonlySet<string>,
  isKnownToRoom: (elementId: string) => boolean,
  now = Date.now(),
): T[] =>
  localElements.filter(
    (element) =>
      !element.isDeleted &&
      !roomElementIds.has(element.id) &&
      isKnownToRoom(element.id) &&
      isPastDeletionExpiry(element, now),
  );
```

```typescript
import { newElement } from "@excalidraw/element";

import type { ExcalidrawElement } from "@excalidraw/element/types";

import { DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT } from "../app_constants";
import {
  getExpiredResurrections,
  getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion,
  isPastDeletionExpiry,
} from "../collab/expiredDeletions";

const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 12);
const OLD = NOW - DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT - 1;
const RECENT = NOW - 1000;

const element = (
  id: string,
  updated: number,
  isDeleted = false,
): ExcalidrawElement => ({
  ...newElement({ type: "rectangle", x: 0, y: 0 }),
  id,
  updated,
  isDeleted,
});

describe("isPastDeletionExpiry", () => {
  it("is true only for changes older than the deletion timeout", () => {
    expect(isPastDeletionExpiry(element("a", OLD), NOW)).toBe(true);
    expect(
      isPastDeletionExpiry(element("a", NOW - DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT), NOW),
    ).toBe(false);
    expect(isPastDeletionExpiry(element("a", RECENT), NOW)).toBe(false);
  });

  it("works with hybrid logical clock timestamps (fractional ms)", () => {
    expect(isPastDeletionExpiry(element("a", OLD + 0.5), NOW)).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("getExpiredResurrections (receiving an update)", () => {
  it("ignores an old live element this client doesn't have", () => {
    const stale = element("stale", OLD);
    expect(getExpiredResurrections([stale], new Map(), NOW)).toEqual(
      new Set(["stale"]),
    );
  });

  it("accepts elements this client has, recent ones and deletes", () => {
    const known = element("known", OLD);
    const recent = element("recent", RECENT);
    const deleted = element("deleted", OLD, true);
    expect(
      getExpiredResurrections(
        [known, recent, deleted],
        new Map([["known", known]]),
        NOW,
      ),
    ).toEqual(new Set());
  });
});

describe("getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion (against the stored scene)", () => {
  const knownToRoom = (ids: string[]) => (id: string) => ids.includes(id);

  it("finds old live elements the room had but no longer has", () => {
    const stale = element("stale", OLD);
    expect(
      getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion(
        [stale],
        new Set(),
        knownToRoom(["stale"]),
        NOW,
      ).map((el) => el.id),
    ).toEqual(["stale"]);
  });

  it("keeps elements still in the room", () => {
    const live = element("live", OLD);
    expect(
      getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion(
        [live],
        new Set(["live"]),
        knownToRoom(["live"]),
        NOW,
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("keeps elements the room never saw (e.g. drawn offline)", () => {
    const offline = element("offline", OLD);
    expect(
      getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion(
        [offline],
        new Set(),
        () => false,
        NOW,
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("keeps recently changed elements (not yet saved)", () => {
    const recent = element("recent", RECENT);
    expect(
      getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion(
        [recent],
        new Set(),
        knownToRoom(["recent"]),
        NOW,
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("ignores elements that are already deleted", () => {
    const deleted = element("deleted", OLD, true);
    expect(
      getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion(
        [deleted],
        new Set(),
        knownToRoom(["deleted"]),
        NOW,
      ),
    ).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

All three pieces are in place. Typecheck and lint are clean. The full suite has 2376 passing and 2 failing, and neither failure is caused by these changes:

Nothing is committed.

One correction first. Earlier I said a logical counter would fix the clock-skew case (case 5), clients that haven't exchanged anything yet. That was wrong. No clock can order changes made at the same time on two devices whose clocks disagree before they've communicated. The counter fixes a different gap, described below, and the comment in `clock.ts` now says what it can't do.

## 1. Dragging and multi-element transforms

- **One edit can now cover several elements.** The registry in `inProgressEdit.ts` stores each edited element with the timestamp it had when the gesture started (taken from `pointerDownState.originalElements`, from before the first move).
- **Which elements are included:** the selection, its labels, its frame children, and arrows bound to it, since a drag reroutes them.
- **Remote changes:** a newer remote change to a dragged or transformed element is merged in for every property the gesture doesn't own:

  - both a drag and a transform own the geometry;
  - a drag also owns `frameId`.

  So a recolour made during your drag survives, and the drag keeps moving the element.

- **Remote deletes:**
  - **Drag:** the deleted element drops out and the rest keep moving. Dragging already skips deleted elements, so nothing jumps.
  - **Transform:** the gesture is cancelled, because scaling uses the selection's starting bounds and dropping one element would make the others jump.
  - **Both:** the delete is re-issued with a later timestamp, and a notice is shown.
- **Tests:** 6 new ones in `inProgressEdit.test.tsx`. I confirmed the drag tests fail when drag tracking is switched off.

## 2. Logical counter (`packages/common/src/clock.ts`)

- **What it fixes:** every local change is now strictly newer than anything the clock has seen. Before, a change made after seeing a remote change in the same millisecond could tie with it and fall back to the version rule.
- **How it's stored:** in the same `updated` number, as `ms + counter/1024`. That's exact in a JavaScript number until about the year 2248, needs no format change, and older clients and expiry checks still read it as milliseconds. After 1024 changes within one millisecond, the clock moves on to the next millisecond.

## 3. Elements whose deletion expired no longer come back (`excalidraw-app/collab/expiredDeletions.ts`)

The web app stops syncing deleted elements 24 hours after deletion. The rule I used: a live element is synced within seconds of every change. So if the room's stored scene lacks a live element that this client has synced before, and the element hasn't changed in over 24 hours, its deletion expired.

- **When saving and after each save:** your stale live copies are left out of what's saved to Firebase, and get deleted locally. That fresh delete is broadcast to other clients that may hold stale copies too.
- **When receiving an update:** old live elements you don't have are ignored. Their age is measured with the **sender's** clock, which now sends its current time with each update (`sentAt`, an optional field older clients don't send).
- **Why the sender's clock:** my first version used the receiving client's clock, and it broke 7 collaboration tests. That exposed a real bug: a peer whose clock was more than 24 hours _behind_ would have had every new element it drew rejected.
- **Edge cases:**
  - Elements this client never synced, for example drawn while offline, are always kept.
  - If the sender runs older code (no `sentAt`), the receiving check is skipped, and the save-time check still catches the element.
  - Remaining risk: if a live element's Firebase saves failed for more than 24 hours, it can be treated as an expired deletion. Some peers may not see it until the next successful save brings it back.
- **Tests:** 11 unit tests for these rules. There's no end-to-end test that drives a full room, an offline tab, and Firebase.

```markdown
**Not tested automatically, and why:** None of AC-A, AC-B or AC-C was checked only by hand; all three have automated tests. No manual check was done for any criterion. Not covered by any test, automated or manual:

- **Real collaboration between clients.** Two browsers in one room with the relay server and Firebase. The tests simulate remote updates by calling `reconcileElements` directly, so they don't exercise Collab, Portal or the socket and Firebase code paths.
- **Visibility on the canvas (AC-B).** It is tested only at the unit level (`isElementByHiddenCreator` and `isElementInteractive`). No test renders a co-owned element and checks that it's drawn or hidden.
- **"Drawing clusters" (AC-A).** Co-ownership is recorded per element. Labels follow their shape (tested), but there's no specific test that editing a group co-owns every member.
- **The expiry wiring.** No test drives an offline tab for more than 24 hours. The rules themselves are unit-tested, but their integration into `Collab.tsx` and `firebase.ts` is not.

**AI-written tests:** All tests in the five files listed above were written by AI (Claude) during this work. The existing test in `reconcile.test.ts` was not modified. Two of the files were later changed by AI when the co-owner data format gained counters and removal markers: after an undo, the expected co-owner list became `[]` with a removal marker instead of "missing". That change follows from the design decision that removals must be kept so that stale copies lose; it was not copied from the code's output.

How the expected values were checked:

1. Expected values were derived from the acceptance criteria and the rules in the issue discussion (for example, the Alice/Bob/Carol example and the undo rule), or worked out by hand from each test's inputs. They were not copied from the code's output.
2. Several tests were shown to be able to fail:
   - With the in-progress-edit merge turned off, 6 of the 11 tests in `inProgressEdit.test.tsx` failed (before the drag/transform tests were added).
   - With drag tracking turned off, all 4 drag tests failed.
   - The first version of the co-ownership integration tests failed (8 of 10) because arrow-key moves aren't saved as their own undo step; they were changed to use a stroke-width change.
   - A first version of the expiry check broke 7 existing collaboration tests, which exposed a real clock-skew bug that was then fixed.
3. Not done: no feature-disabled check like the ones in step 2 was run on the AC-A/B/C co-ownership tests, and no person has reviewed the expected values yet. Review them before merging.

Full suite at the time of writing: typecheck and lint clean; 2376 passed, 2 failed. `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx` was already failing before this work. `pathMotionConfig.test.tsx` is an animation-timing test that passes when run alone, so it looks like a flake under full-suite load.
```

<pasted_content id="4a55"> Closes #61

## Why

Issue #61 (child of #37). If a user wanted to add filters then providing a menu that acts as a complete control panel helps streamline and understand the new feature. So this subissue aimed to create a menu that allowed for that. Provides many feature aimed a quick and intuitive image filter application.

## What changed

- **Data model:** `ExcalidrawImageElement.filter: "grayscale" | null` is replaced by:
  - `filters: ImageFilterEntry[]`: an ordered stack, at most one entry per type, always in UI order (grayscale, then color shift).
  - `adjustments: ImageAdjustments | null`: per-image brightness, contrast and saturation, applied after the filter stack. `null` means defaults.
- **New module `packages/element/src/imageFilters.ts`:** the single source of truth for filter definitions.
  - Defines each property's min, max, step and default. Everything is 0–1 today, but the bounds are not hardcoded, so a future 1–100 property only needs a new definition.
  - Provides the clamping and validation helpers.
  - Generates the CSS filter strings and the matching per-pixel math (W3C Filter Effects matrices) used as the fallback on Safari.
- **Color shift filter:**
  - A hue slider (0–1 → 0–360°) with an intensity slider and a color swatch.
  - On its own it is a hue rotation.
  - When applied on top of grayscale, it tints the gray image toward the chosen hue (sepia, then hue-rotate, then saturate). A plain hue rotation has no visible effect on gray pixels.
- **Rendering:** the canvas renderer, SVG export and Safari pixel fallback all use the shared module. The element canvas cache now keys on the full filter state, so every slider change re-renders the image.
- **Restore:** old scenes with `filter: "grayscale"` are migrated to the new stack. Unknown or duplicate filter types are dropped, and invalid or out-of-range values are clamped or reset to defaults.
- **UI:** a new "Image filters" section in the left properties panel (`ImageFiltersPanel.tsx`), shown only when exactly one image is selected. It has:
  - an "Add filter" dropdown
  - for each filter: a dropdown to swap its type, plus reset and remove buttons and sliders
  - an Adjustments group with its own reset button
- **Copy/paste filters:** new `copyImageFilters` and `pasteImageFilters` actions. Paste replaces the filters and adjustments wholesale on every selected image.
- **Removed:** the standalone "Apply grayscale" button, from both the desktop and compact action lists. The `toggleImageGrayscale` action still exists (for example in the command palette) and now adds oving other filters alone.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced

- Color shift has two modes: a hue rotation on its own, and a tint when grayscale is applied before it. The tint uses an approximate sepia base hue (`SEPIA_HUE = 38`), and the strength (`saturate(300%)` at full intensity) was not tuned visually.
- Each slider `onChange` is captured as its own history entry (`CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY`, the same as the existing opacity slider). One drag can therefore create several undo steps.
- Compact mode (small screens) has no filter panel. It only has the copy/paste filter buttons.
- Copied filter settings live in a module-level variable, not the system clipboard. They are lost on reload and can't be shared between tabs.
- Swapping a filter's type resets the new filter to its default values; properties are not carried over.
- New UI strings were added to `en.json` only.

### Encountered

- Vitest also collects tests from the stray `.tmp-ai-logs-wt/` checkout, which shows up as failures that are not real and rewrites snapshots inside that folder.
- jsdom converts every CSS `hsl()` color to black, so the hue swatch's actual color can't be checked in tests.

```markdown
Closes #<issue>

## Why

Issue #<issue> (child of #<parent>). Hiding and locking collaborators (#81) was based only on who _created_ an element. Once someone edited another person's element, the element still followed only its creator's visibility and lock settings, so a collaborator you had chosen to keep visible could have their work hidden or locked away. This issue makes everyone who edits an element its co-owner, and makes the element follow the least restricted of its owners: it stays visible, and editable, as long as at least one co-owner is.

Working through how co-ownership behaves in a live room exposed several sync problems, which this PR also fixes:

- Conflicting edits were decided by "the copy changed the most times wins", so a long drag beat a later delete.
- Concurrent co-owner stamps could overwrite each other.
- Changes from other users made during your drag, resize or text edit were silently dropped.
- Elements whose deletion was older than 24 hours could come back.

## What changed

- **Co-ownership data:** `customData.creatorId` still records the creator. New fields:
  - `customData.editorIds`: the current co-owners.
  - `customData.editorSeqs`: a counter per client, bumped each time that client is added or removed. It makes the co-owner list mergeable: only each client changes its own entry, so the higher counter is the newer state, and a removed co-owner keeps their counter as a marker so an older copy can't add them back.
- **Becoming a co-owner (`packages/element/src/ownership.ts`, `packages/element/src/store.ts`, `App.tsx`):**
  - A new `Store.onBeforeDurableCaptureEmitter` fires just before a local change is saved to undo history.
  - At that point, `getElementsToCoOwn` finds elements the user edited directly (selected, or text being edited) but doesn't own, and stamps the user as a co-owner as part of the **same undo step**.
  - Side effects don't count: rerouted arrows, frame children, z-order, `boundElements`.
  - Editing a label co-owns its shape.
- **Least-restricted-owner rule:**

  - `isElementByHiddenCreator`: an element is hidden only if **every** owner is hidden.
  - `isElementInteractive`: it can be interacted with if **any** owner is interactive.

  Rendering, hit testing, selection, the eraser, export, search and arrow binding all go through these two functions, so all of them follow the new rule. "Hide all" and the per-row drawing counts include co-owners.

- **Undo/redo (`packages/excalidraw/history.ts`):**
  - Undoing every edit a user made to an element removes them as a co-owner; redo adds them back.
  - Undo/redo normally restores the whole `customData` object. A merge step now keeps other clients' co-ownership as it was, so only the current user's entry follows history.
- **Latest change wins (`packages/common/src/clock.ts`, `packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`):**
  - A hybrid logical clock stamps `updated`: it follows the wall clock, never goes backwards, has a logical counter for changes within the same millisecond, and jumps forward when it sees a newer remote timestamp (capped at 60 s ahead of the local clock).
  - It's stored in the same `updated` number as `ms + counter/1024`, so the format doesn't change.
  - Reconcile now keeps the copy with the later timestamp. It falls back to the old version/nonce rules for same-millisecond changes and for old data without timestamps.
  - Co-owner lists are merged from both copies instead of being taken from the winner.
- **Incoming changes during edits in progress (new module `packages/excalidraw/data/inProgressEdit.ts`):**

  - Covers resizing or rotating one element, text editing, drawing a new element, dragging, and multi-element transforms.
  - Each edit owns some properties: geometry for all of them, plus the text for a text edit and `frameId` for a drag. A newer remote change to any _other_ property is merged into the local element. For example, a recolour made during your drag survives.
  - A newer remote delete:

    - **text edit, single-element resize, drawing, multi-element transform:** cancels the edit;
    - **drag:** removes just that element, and the rest keep moving.

    Either way, the editor re-issues the delete with a later timestamp so it sticks, and shows a notice.

  - Stale copies made before the edit started are ignored.
  - To support cancelling, the text editor now returns `{ submit, cancel }`, and `App` keeps a reference to the active pointer gesture.

- **Expired deletions (new module `excalidraw-app/collab/expiredDeletions.ts`):** deleted elements stop syncing 24 hours after deletion.
  - **The rule:** a live element the room's stored scene doesn't have, which this client synced before, and which hasn't changed in over 24 hours, was deleted.
  - **When saving to Firebase:** such elements are left out of the save and deleted locally.
  - **When receiving an update:** old live elements this client doesn't have are ignored. Age is measured with the sender's clock, via a new optional `sentAt` field on scene updates, so a client whose clock is far behind can still add elements.
- **Strings:** `collaboratorEdit.deletedWhileEditing` added to `en.json`.

## Tech Debt

### Introduced

- **One edit per page:** the in-progress-edit registry (`inProgressEdit.ts`) and the element clock (`elementClock`) are module-level singletons. Two Excalidraw editors on the same page would share them.
- **Co-owner removal markers are never cleaned up.** `editorSeqs` keeps an entry for every client that ever co-owned an element.
- **Fractional timestamps:** `updated` can now have a fractional part. External tools that assume whole milliseconds will see fractions. The encoding is exact until about the year 2248.
- **Deploy all clients together:** clients running the old rule and the new rule can settle on different copies of a conflicting element. Reloading the page fixes it.
- **Edits not covered by the in-progress handling:** line/arrow point editing, cropping and arrow-key nudges still use plain "latest change wins". During those continuous edits, remote changes are mostly lost.
- **Cancelling an edit loses work:**
  - Cancelling a multi-element transform leaves the other elements where they were mid-gesture. Nothing is rolled back, and they're only recorded in undo with the next change.
  - Cancelling a text edit loses the text typed so far.
- **The delete notice doesn't say who deleted the element**, and the new string is in `en.json` only.
- **Expiry false positive:** a live element whose Firebase saves failed for over 24 hours can be treated as an expired deletion. Some peers may not see it until the next successful save brings it back.
- **Clock skew isn't solved:** changes made at the same time on two devices whose clocks disagree, before they've exchanged anything, are still ordered by those clocks. The 60 s cap limits how far a wrong clock can push others.

### Encountered

- **Arrow-key moves aren't saved as their own undo step;** they're folded into the next one. This also delays co-ownership from an arrow-key move until that next step.
- **The text editor and pointer gestures had no way to cancel.** Both were added for this PR.
- **`getUpdatedTimestamp()` returns `1` in tests.** Every existing test therefore runs on the version fallback, and the new time-ordering tests set timestamps explicitly.
- **Test failures not caused by this PR:**
  - `pathPlaybackHold.test.tsx` (an untracked file in the working tree, not part of this PR) was already failing before this work.
  - `pathMotionConfig.test.tsx` ("a 300px path at 0.5x speed plays for 2000ms") and `history.test.tsx` ("should create new history entry on scene import via drag&drop") failed once each under full-suite load and passed when run alone.
- **Remote updates during a gesture update the store snapshot mid-gesture,** so that gesture's undo step can be partial. This was already the case for drags and is unchanged by this PR.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: Joint ownership tracking | `coOwnership.test.tsx`: "editing a collaborator's element adds me as a co-owner, keeping the creator", "selecting without editing doesn't", "editing my own element doesn't add me as a co-owner", "a co-owned element counts for each owner in the menu"; `coOwnership.test.ts` (element): "a selected, edited element someone else created gets me as co-owner", "an element changed as a side effect (not selected) doesn't", "elements I already own don't", "new, deleted, unstamped or merely re-indexed elements don't", "editing a label co-owns its shape", "does nothing outside of a room (no self id)", "moving or restyling is an edit", "bookkeeping, z-order and binding references are not", "lists the creator first, then co-owners, without duplicates", "bound text follows its container's owners", "keeps concurrent co-owners from both copies", "is commutative: both orders give the same co-owners"; `reconcileClock.test.ts`: "concurrent co-owner stamps both survive, whichever copy wins" | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion |
| B: Shared visibility evaluation | `coOwnership.test.tsx` › "visibility of a co-owned element (rendering, AC-B)": "(control) without co-owners, hiding the creator hides the element", "after I edit it, hiding its creator keeps it on my canvas and in exports", "it's hidden once every one of its co-owners is hidden", "a peer's co-owned element stays visible while any co-owner is visible", "shows again as soon as one co-owner is shown again"; also "once I co-own it, locking its creator doesn't lock it for me", "without co-owning, locking its creator deselects it (unchanged)"; `coOwnership.test.ts` › "least restricted owner rule" (7 tests, including "Bob locked, Carol not → interactive for Alice" and "Bob hidden, Carol visible → visible and interactive") | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion (the Alice/Bob/Carol example) |
| C: Dynamic ownership updates | `coOwnership.test.tsx`: "editing it again doesn't add me twice", "undoing my only edit removes me as a co-owner, redo adds me back", "I stay a co-owner until ALL my edits to the element are undone", "undo keeps co-owners other clients added in the meantime", "undoing an unrelated edit doesn't touch my co-ownership"; `coOwnership.test.ts` › "reconcileEditorIdsAfterHistory" (5 tests), "getCoOwnedCustomData adds me with a new counter and keeps other custom data", "a newer removal beats an older copy that still lists the co-owner", "a newer re-add beats an older removal"; `reconcileClock.test.ts`: "an undone co-ownership stays removed against a stale copy", "merging into the local winner keeps the same element object" | unit, integration | AC, issue discussion (undo rule) |
| Beyond the ACs: latest change wins | `reconcileClock.test.ts` › "HybridClock" (10 tests), "reconcileElements — the latest change wins" (6 tests, each checking that both clients end up with the same element) | unit | issue discussion; upstream behavior (the version/nonce fallbacks) |
| Beyond the ACs: incoming changes during edits | `inProgressEdit.test.tsx`: "getMergeableRemoteChanges" (2), "while resizing" (7), "while editing text" (2), "while dragging" (4), "while transforming several elements" (2) | integration | issue discussion; numbers such as `width` 130 and `x` 20 worked out by hand from the pointer moves |
| Beyond the ACs: expired deletions | `expiredDeletions.test.ts`: "isPastDeletionExpiry" (2), "getExpiredResurrections" (4), "getLocalElementsWithExpiredDeletion" (5) | unit | issue discussion; existing `DELETED_ELEMENT_TIMEOUT` (24 h) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- No criterion was checked only by hand, and no manual checks were done.
- Real collaboration between two browsers (relay server and Firebase) isn't covered. The tests apply remote updates through `reconcileElements` or `updateScene` directly, so Collab, Portal and the socket/Firebase code paths aren't exercised.
- Groups as "drawing clusters" (AC-A) have no dedicated test. Co-ownership is per element, so editing a group stamps each edited member, but no test checks that.
- The expiry rules are unit-tested, but their wiring into `Collab.tsx` and `firebase.ts` is not. No test simulates a tab offline for more than 24 hours.
```
